docs.title: flow_inference
docs.text:
Guided flow-based sampling of stochastic processes under user-specified conditions.

flow_inference draws samples of a stochastic process — a Gaussian process, an SDE solution, or anything a neural flow can be trained on — that satisfy a condition you supply: an ODE or PDE residual, a shape constraint such as monotonicity, a point-process likelihood, and so on. It does this by integrating a probability-flow ODE (or SDE) from noise to the process, steering each step with a guidance term computed from the condition's log-likelihood.

Want to see the examples run? The notebooks in this repo are stored without outputs. Browse them fully executed, with every figure, at https://flowinference.github.io/flow-inference/.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install -e .                  # the library
pip install -e ".[examples]"      # plus what the example notebooks need

Requires Python 3.12+. The library depends only on torch, gpytorch and tqdm.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Sample functions from a GP prior, conditioned to average to 1 over the domain:

import gpytorch
import torch

from flow_inference.conditions import EqualityCondition
from flow_inference.flow_utils import build_grid_in_box
from flow_inference.flows import GaussianProcessFlow
from flow_inference.guidance import GuidanceMC
from flow_inference.sampler import IntegratorSampler

torch.set_default_dtype(torch.float64)

# A GP prior on 128 points in [0, 1].
grid = build_grid_in_box(128, 1)
kernel = gpytorch.kernels.ScaleKernel(gpytorch.kernels.RBFKernel())
kernel.base_kernel.lengthscale = 0.1
flow = GaussianProcessFlow(kernel, gpytorch.means.ZeroMean(), grid)


# Condition: the sampled function must average to 1 over the domain.
class MeanIsOne(EqualityCondition):
    def residual(self, x):  # x: (batch, channels, points)
        return x.mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True) - 1.0


guidance = GuidanceMC(flow, MeanIsOne(sigma=1e-2), num_mc_samples=10)
samples = IntegratorSampler(flow).sample(16, guidance=guidance, num_steps=500)
# samples: (16, 1, 128), each averaging ~1

To condition on data as well, build the flow from a GP posterior instead: mean, kernel = gp_posterior(kernel, X, y) from flow_inference.gp_utils.

docs.title: Package layout
docs.text: Module Contents flows The flows to sample from: GaussianFlow, GaussianProcessFlow (function space), BasisGaussianProcessFlow (weight space), GaussianIncrementFlow, NeuralFlow (learned) conditions What samples should satisfy: EqualityCondition (residuals), BinaryCondition (inequalities), PointWiseCondition, ProductCondition guidance How the condition steers sampling: GuidanceDPS, GuidanceMPGD, GuidanceMC, GuidanceMCFisher, GuidanceEnsembleKalman sampler IntegratorSampler (ODE/SDE integration) and PCNCorrector (gradient-free MCMC correction) mcmc Baselines on the same latent target, run directly on the N(0, I) innovations: preconditioned Crank–Nicolson (pcn), elliptical slice sampling (elliptical_slice), Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (hmc) and likelihood-tempered SMC (tempered_smc, which also estimates the evidence) gp_utils GP posteriors, kernel fitting, and random-Fourier-feature bases maps, training_samplers Non-Gaussian spatial processes (Student-t, Brown–Resnick, Lévy–NIG, ...) as maps from Gaussian noise, and the training data they provide for NeuralFlow schedules, flow_utils Noise schedules and grid helpers

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
Install the development tools and the pre-commit hooks (--group needs pip 25.1+, or use uv sync):

pip install -e . --group dev
pre-commit install --install-hooks        # ruff + notebook output stripping on commit
pre-commit install --hook-type pre-push   # test suite must pass before push

Notebooks are committed with their outputs stripped (via nbstripout). To publish the rendered notebooks, execute them at full budget (a GPU helps) and deploy the site to the gh-pages branch, which keeps a single commit:

pip install -e ".[examples]" --group dev --group docs
python scripts/build_docs.py              # runs new/changed notebooks into build/docs
mkdocs serve                              # preview locally
mkdocs gh-deploy --force --no-history     # publish

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
pytest               # fast suite
pytest -m slow       # slow tests only
pytest -m notebooks  # smoke-run every example notebook (about a minute on CPU)

The notebook smoke tests execute each notebook with capped sampling and training budgets, so they check that the examples run, not that their results are good.

class AllenCahnCondition(EqualityCondition):
    def __init__(self, sigma=10.0, eps=1e-4):
        super().__init__(sigma=sigma)
        self.register_buffer("eps", torch.tensor(float(eps)))

    def residual(self, x):  # (B, 1, H*W) -> (B, 1, H*(W-2))
        u = self.as_grid(x)[:, 0]  # (B, H, W)
        B, H, W = u.shape
        dt = 1.0 / W
        dx = 2.0 / H  # periodic grid: x_i = -1 + i*dx, and x = 1 wraps to x = -1

        u_t = (u[:, :, 2:] - u[:, :, :-2]) / (2.0 * dt)  # central difference, interior times
        u_xx = (u.roll(-1, dims=1) - 2.0 * u + u.roll(1, dims=1)) / dx**2  # periodic in x
        u_int = u[:, :, 1:-1]
        residual = u_t - self.eps * u_xx[:, :, 1:-1] + 5.0 * (u_int.pow(3) - u_int)
        return residual.reshape(B, 1, -1)

docs.title: Allen–Cahn PDE conditioning of a Gaussian process¶
docs.text:
We fit a Gaussian process (GP) to sparse, early-time observations of a solution to the Allen–Cahn equation

\[u_t = \epsilon\, u_{xx} + 5\,(u - u^3), \qquad x \in [-1, 1],\ t \in [0, 1],\]

and then use guided flow sampling to draw fields from the GP posterior that also approximately satisfy the PDE with periodic boundary conditions. The data only constrain \(t < 0.28\); the physics conditions shape the samples at later times without any extra observations.

docs.title: 2. Load data¶
docs.text: The training set is NUM_TRAIN points drawn at random from the early-time part of the reference solution. Space is rescaled from \([-1, 1]\) to \([0, 1]\) so both inputs live in the unit box used by the sampling grid. The grid's \(H\) points \(x_i = -1 + 2i/H\) stop one step short of \(x = 1\), which is the periodic image of \(x = -1\).

docs.title: 3. GP posterior¶
docs.text: We fit the hyperparameters of an anisotropic RBF kernel (separate space and time lengthscales) by type-II maximum likelihood, then hand the conjugate posterior mean and kernel to a GaussianProcessFlow on an \(H \times W\) grid. Unguided samples are draws from this data-only posterior.

docs.title: 4. Physics condition¶
docs.text: The PDE is imposed as an EqualityCondition on the finite-difference residual \(u_t - \epsilon u_{xx} + 5u^3 - 5u\), which should be zero. \(u_t\) is a central difference, so the residual is evaluated at every interior time; \(u_{xx}\) uses a stencil that wraps around in \(x\), which imposes the periodic boundary conditions exactly with no separate boundary term. as_grid views the flat field as \((B, C, H, W)\), with the grid shape taken from the flow when the condition is passed to the guidance.

docs.title: 5. Physics-guided sampling¶
docs.text: The condition is enforced with Monte Carlo guidance during SDE sampling from the same GP posterior flow.

def build_grid(H, W, device):
    """(H*W, 2) unit-box coordinates; space includes both ends, so x = 2*c - 1 spans [-1, 1]."""
    xs = torch.linspace(0.0, 1.0, H, device=device)
    ts = torch.arange(W, device=device) / W
    xx, tt = torch.meshgrid(xs, ts, indexing="ij")
    return torch.stack([xx, tt], dim=-1).view(-1, 2)

BurgersCondition evaluates the PDE residual by centred differences at the interior grid points, and a PointWiseCondition pins the first and last spatial rows to zero at all times. ProductCondition imposes both.

In [5]: Copied! 
class BurgersCondition(EqualityCondition):
    """Burgers residual by finite differences, for a single-channel field in (H, W) order."""

    def __init__(self, H, W, sigma=10.0):
        super().__init__(sigma=sigma)
        self.H = H
        self.W = W
        self.dx = 2.0 / (H - 1)  # the grid includes x = -1 and x = 1
        self.dt = 1.0 / W
        self.nu = 0.02  # viscosity

    def residual(self, x):  # x: (B, 1, H*W)
        B, C, N = x.shape
        assert C == 1, f"Expected C=1, got C={C}"
        assert N == self.H * self.W, f"Expected N={self.H*self.W}, got N={N}"

        u = x.view(B, self.H, self.W)
        u_int = u[:, 1:-1, 1:-1]  # interior points, (B, H-2, W-2)
        du_dt = (u[:, 1:-1, 2:] - u[:, 1:-1, :-2]) / (2.0 * self.dt)
        du_dx = (u[:, 2:, 1:-1] - u[:, :-2, 1:-1]) / (2.0 * self.dx)
        d2u_dx2 = (u[:, 2:, 1:-1] - 2.0 * u_int + u[:, :-2, 1:-1]) / (self.dx * self.dx)
        res = du_dt + u_int * du_dx - self.nu * d2u_dx2
        return res.reshape(B, 1, -1)  # (B, 1, (H-2)*(W-2))


def dirichlet_mask(H, W):
    # True on the first and last spatial rows (x = -1 and x = 1), for all times.
    mask = torch.zeros((H, W), dtype=torch.bool)
    mask[0, :] = True
    mask[-1, :] = True
    return mask.view(-1)  # (H*W,)
class BurgersCondition(EqualityCondition): """Burgers residual by finite differences, for a single-channel field in (H, W) order.""" def __init__(self, H, W, sigma=10.0): super().__init__(sigma=sigma) self.H = H self.W = W self.dx = 2.0 / (H - 1) # the grid includes x = -1 and x = 1 self.dt = 1.0 / W self.nu = 0.02 # viscosity def residual(self, x): # x: (B, 1, H*W) B, C, N = x.shape assert C == 1, f"Expected C=1, got C={C}" assert N == self.H * self.W, f"Expected N={self.H*self.W}, got N={N}" u = x.view(B, self.H, self.W) u_int = u[:, 1:-1, 1:-1] # interior points, (B, H-2, W-2) du_dt = (u[:, 1:-1, 2:] - u[:, 1:-1, :-2]) / (2.0 * self.dt) du_dx = (u[:, 2:, 1:-1] - u[:, :-2, 1:-1]) / (2.0 * self.dx) d2u_dx2 = (u[:, 2:, 1:-1] - 2.0 * u_int + u[:, :-2, 1:-1]) / (self.dx * self.dx) res = du_dt + u_int * du_dx - self.nu * d2u_dx2 return res.reshape(B, 1, -1) # (B, 1, (H-2)*(W-2)) def dirichlet_mask(H, W): # True on the first and last spatial rows (x = -1 and x = 1), for all times. mask = torch.zeros((H, W), dtype=torch.bool) mask[0, :] = True mask[-1, :] = True return mask.view(-1) # (H*W,) In [6]: Copied! 
pde_condition = BurgersCondition(H, W, sigma=1e-5).to(device)
boundary_condition = PointWiseCondition(
    torch.zeros(H * W, device=device), dirichlet_mask(H, W), sigma=1e-6).to(device)
condition = ProductCondition([pde_condition, boundary_condition]).to(device)
guidance = GuidanceMC(flow, condition, num_mc_samples=1).to(device)
samples = sampler.sample(num_samples, guidance=guidance, num_steps=1_000)

class BurgersWeightCondition(EqualityCondition):
    """Burgers residual in weight space, using the basis's analytic derivatives."""

    def __init__(self, basis, grid, H, W, sigma=10.0):
        super().__init__(sigma=sigma)
        self.nu = 0.02  # viscosity
        sx = 0.5  # d/dx = sx * d/dcoord, since x = 2*coord - 1

        interior = torch.zeros((H, W), dtype=torch.bool)
        interior[1:-1, 1:-1] = True
        interior = interior.view(-1)  # (N,)

        self.phi = basis.phi(grid)[:, interior]  # (R, A)
        self.dphi_dx = sx * basis.compute_derivative(grid, (0,), (1,))[:, interior]
        self.dphi_dx2 = sx**2 * basis.compute_derivative(grid, (0,), (2,))[:, interior]
        self.dphi_dt = basis.compute_derivative(grid, (1,), (1,))[:, interior]

        self.mean = basis.mean(grid)[interior]  # (A,)
        self.dmean_dx = sx * basis.mean_derivative(grid, (0,), (1,))[interior]
        self.dmean_dx2 = sx**2 * basis.mean_derivative(grid, (0,), (2,))[interior]
        self.dmean_dt = basis.mean_derivative(grid, (1,), (1,))[interior]

    def residual(self, w):  # w: (B, 1, R)
        f = w @ self.phi + self.mean
        f_x = w @ self.dphi_dx + self.dmean_dx
        f_xx = w @ self.dphi_dx2 + self.dmean_dx2
        f_t = w @ self.dphi_dt + self.dmean_dt
        return f_t + f * f_x - self.nu * f_xx  # (B, 1, A)


class PointWiseWeightCondition(EqualityCondition):
    """Pin the field to a target at masked grid points, in weight space."""

    def __init__(self, target_field, mask, basis, grid, sigma=1e-6):
        super().__init__(sigma=sigma)
        self.target_field = target_field
        self.mask = mask
        self.phi = basis.phi(grid)
        self.mean = basis.mean(grid)

    def residual(self, w):  # w: (B, 1, R)
        f = w @ self.phi + self.mean
        return f[:, :, self.mask] - self.target_field[self.mask]

def _sync():
    if device == "cuda":
        torch.cuda.synchronize()  # time the work, not the asynchronous launch


def run_function_space(H, W):
    crd = build_grid(H, W, device)
    _sync(); t0 = time.perf_counter()
    mu, kk = gp_posterior(kernel, X_initial, Y_initial, noise=noise)
    fl = GaussianProcessFlow(kk, mu, crd, device=device)  # O(N^3) Cholesky, O(N^2) storage
    _sync(); t_setup = time.perf_counter() - t0

        BurgersCondition(H, W, sigma=1e-5),
        PointWiseCondition(torch.zeros(H * W, device=device), dirichlet_mask(H, W), sigma=1e-6),
    ]).to(device)
    gd = GuidanceMC(fl, cond, num_mc_samples=1).to(device)

    _sync(); t0 = time.perf_counter()
    out = IntegratorSampler(flow=fl).sample(num_samples, guidance=gd, num_steps=BENCH_STEPS, verbose=False)
    _sync()
    return t_setup, time.perf_counter() - t0, out.reshape(num_samples, 1, H * W)

docs.title: Burgers Equation: Function Space vs Weight Space¶
docs.text:
This notebook conditions a space-time GP on the viscous Burgers PDE

\[u_t + u\,u_x = \nu\,u_{xx}, \qquad \nu = 0.02,\]

with zero Dirichlet boundaries, starting from a GP posterior given a few noisy observations of a sine initial condition. It does so two ways: a function-space flow over the \(N = H \times W\) grid values, with the residual formed by finite differences, and an RFF weight-space flow over \(R\) random-Fourier-feature weights, whose basis functions have analytic derivatives. The last section shows how the wall time of each scales with \(N\).

docs.title: 2. Configuration¶
docs.text: The unit grid maps to space \(x \in [-1, 1]\) along \(H\) and time \(t \in [0, 1)\) along \(W\). The space axis includes both endpoints, so the Dirichlet conditions can be pinned at \(x = \pm 1\) exactly; the spacing is \(\Delta x = 2 / (H - 1)\).

docs.title: 3. Function-Space Flow¶
docs.text: The GP has an anisotropic RBF kernel, set by hand, conditioned on noisy observations of \(u(x, 0) = -\sin(\pi x)\). That posterior is the flow's starting distribution, before any PDE conditioning.

docs.title: 4. RFF Weight-Space Flow¶
docs.text: Same problem, but the diffusion runs over basis weights rather than the \(N\) grid values, and the initial condition enters through a conditioned basis rather than a constraint. DecoupledRFFBasis implements pathwise conditioning (Wilson et al., 2020). The latent width becomes \(R_f + M\), where the extra \(M\) features carry the \(M\) initial condition evaluations.

docs.title: 5. Cost¶
docs.text:
Both flows are run at increasing grid size \(N = H \times W\) (\(W\) fixed, \(H\) growing), with num_steps=250.

  • Function space pays an \(\mathcal{O}(N^3)\) Cholesky once, stores the \((N, N)\) factor, and then pays an \(\mathcal{O}(N^2)\) matmul per step.
  • Weight space keeps a state of width \(R_f + M\), so its cost is linear in \(N\).

from flow_inference.flow_utils import build_grid_in_box
from flow_inference.flows import GaussianProcessFlow
from flow_inference.guidance import GuidanceMC
from flow_inference.sampler import IntegratorSampler

import gpytorch import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import numpy as np import torch from flow_inference.conditions import BaseCondition from flow_inference.flow_utils import build_grid_in_box from flow_inference.flows import GaussianProcessFlow from flow_inference.guidance import GuidanceMC from flow_inference.sampler import IntegratorSampler torch.set_default_dtype(torch.float64) In [2]: Copied! 
device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"

SEED = 1066 if device == "cuda" else 12  # chosen for a clear visual example
T = 10.0            # observation window [0, T]
N = 256             # inference grid points
N_TRUTH = 2000      # fine grid for simulating the ground truth
NUM_SAMPLES = 100
NUM_STEPS = 500

TRUE_LENGTHSCALE = 1.0
TRUE_OUTPUTSCALE = 2.0
TRUE_MEAN = 0.5     # baseline rate exp(0.5) ≈ 1.6 events per unit time

ALPHA = 1.5         # excitation amplitude (known)
BETA = 10.0         # excitation decay rate (known)
device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu" SEED = 1066 if device == "cuda" else 12 # chosen for a clear visual example T = 10.0 # observation window [0, T] N = 256 # inference grid points N_TRUTH = 2000 # fine grid for simulating the ground truth NUM_SAMPLES = 100 NUM_STEPS = 500 TRUE_LENGTHSCALE = 1.0 TRUE_OUTPUTSCALE = 2.0 TRUE_MEAN = 0.5 # baseline rate exp(0.5) ≈ 1.6 events per unit time ALPHA = 1.5 # excitation amplitude (known) BETA = 10.0 # excitation decay rate (known) In [3]: Copied! 
torch.manual_seed(SEED)
t_truth = torch.linspace(0.0, T, N_TRUTH, device=device)

kernel_true = gpytorch.kernels.ScaleKernel(gpytorch.kernels.RBFKernel()).to(device)
kernel_true.base_kernel.lengthscale = TRUE_LENGTHSCALE
kernel_true.outputscale = TRUE_OUTPUTSCALE

with torch.no_grad():
    K_truth = kernel_true(t_truth.unsqueeze(-1)).evaluate()
    L_truth = torch.linalg.cholesky(K_truth + 1e-6 * torch.eye(N_TRUTH, device=device))
    f_truth = TRUE_MEAN + L_truth @ torch.randn(N_TRUTH, device=device)

t_truth_np = t_truth.cpu().numpy()
f_truth_np = f_truth.cpu().numpy()
baseline_truth = torch.exp(f_truth).cpu().numpy()


def simulate_hawkes(baseline, T, alpha, beta, rng):
    # Ogata thinning with the baseline given on a uniform grid over [0, T]
    N_grid = len(baseline)
    dt_grid = T / N_grid
    events = []
    t = 0.0

    while t < T:
        self_excit = sum(alpha * np.exp(-beta * (t - ti)) for ti in events)
        idx_curr = min(int(t / dt_grid), N_grid - 1)
        lambda_star = self_excit + baseline[idx_curr:].max()

        t_cand = t + rng.exponential(1.0 / lambda_star)
        if t_cand >= T:
            break

        # True intensity at the candidate, baseline linearly interpolated
        idx_lo = min(int(t_cand / dt_grid), N_grid - 2)
        frac = (t_cand / dt_grid) - idx_lo
        base_c = (1 - frac) * baseline[idx_lo] + frac * baseline[idx_lo + 1]
        excit_c = sum(alpha * np.exp(-beta * (t_cand - ti)) for ti in events)

        if rng.uniform() < (base_c + excit_c) / lambda_star:
            events.append(t_cand)
        t = t_cand

    return np.array(sorted(events))


rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
ev_np = simulate_hawkes(baseline_truth, T, ALPHA, BETA, rng)

class HawkesCondition(BaseCondition):
    def __init__(self, event_times: torch.Tensor, T: float, N: int, alpha: float, beta: float):
        super().__init__()
        self.register_buffer("dt", torch.tensor(T / N))

        # Excitation at each event from strictly earlier events, H_i
        diff = event_times.unsqueeze(1) - event_times.unsqueeze(0)  # (n, n)
        H = (alpha * torch.exp(-beta * diff) * (diff > 0)).sum(dim=1)  # (n,)
        self.register_buffer("H", H)

        # Integral of the excitation over [0, T], C
        integral_self = (alpha / beta * (1 - torch.exp(-beta * (T - event_times)))).sum()
        self.register_buffer("integral_self", integral_self)

        # Linear interpolation weights of each event onto the grid
        frac_idx = (event_times / T * N).clamp(0.0, N - 1.0 - 1e-9)
        idx_lo = frac_idx.long()
        frac = frac_idx - idx_lo.double()
        self.register_buffer("idx_lo", idx_lo)
        self.register_buffer("w_lo", 1.0 - frac)
        self.register_buffer("w_hi", frac)

    def logp(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        f = x.squeeze(1)  # (B, N)
        f_at_events = self.w_lo * f[:, self.idx_lo] + self.w_hi * f[:, self.idx_lo + 1]  # (B, n)
        event_term = torch.log(torch.exp(f_at_events) + self.H).sum(dim=-1)
        integral_baseline = self.dt * torch.exp(f).sum(dim=-1)
        return event_term - integral_baseline - self.integral_self

docs.title: Hawkes process: inferring a latent baseline intensity via GP flow matching¶
docs.text:
A Hawkes process is a self-exciting point process: each event temporarily raises the rate of future events. We give the baseline a GP prior on its log, \(f \sim \mathcal{GP}(\mu, k)\), and treat the excitation parameters \(\alpha, \beta > 0\) as known:

\[ \lambda(t \mid \mathcal{H}_t) = \underbrace{e^{f(t)}}_{\text{baseline}} + \underbrace{\sum_{t_i < t} \alpha\, e^{-\beta(t - t_i)}}_{\text{self-excitation}}, \qquad \log p(\{t_i\} \mid f) = \sum_{i} \log \lambda(t_i \mid \mathcal{H}_{t_i}) - \int_0^T \lambda(t \mid \mathcal{H}_t)\, \mathrm{d}t. \]

As in the inhomogeneous Poisson (LGCP) notebook, we sample from the GP prior with a flow and guide the samples towards \(p(f \mid \{t_i\})\); the difficulty here is separating the smooth baseline from bursts caused by self-excitation.

docs.title: 2. Simulated data¶
docs.text: Draw \(f^*\) from the GP on a fine grid and simulate events with Ogata's thinning algorithm. Between events the self-excitation only decays, so its current value plus the maximum of the remaining baseline is a valid upper bound on the intensity.

docs.title: 3. GP prior and sampler¶
docs.text: The prior flow lives on an \(N\)-point grid. build_grid_in_box returns coordinates in \([0, 1)\), so the lengthscale is divided by \(T\).

docs.title: 4. Hawkes likelihood¶
docs.text:
Only the baseline depends on \(f\), so everything else is precomputed: the excitation at each event, \(H_i = \sum_{j: t_j < t_i} \alpha e^{-\beta(t_i - t_j)}\), and the closed-form integral of the excitation, \(C = \frac{\alpha}{\beta} \sum_i \bigl(1 - e^{-\beta(T - t_i)}\bigr)\). With \(f(t_i)\) linearly interpolated from the grid, logp evaluates

\[\sum_i \log\bigl(e^{f(t_i)} + H_i\bigr) - \Delta t\sum_j e^{f_j} - C.\]

class ExactPoissonCondition(BaseCondition):
    def __init__(self, event_times: torch.Tensor, T: float, N: int):
        super().__init__()
        self.register_buffer("dt", torch.tensor(T / N))

        # Linear interpolation weights of each event onto the grid
        frac_idx = (event_times / T * N).clamp(0.0, N - 1.0 - 1e-9)
        idx_lo = frac_idx.long()
        frac = frac_idx - idx_lo.double()
        self.register_buffer("idx_lo", idx_lo)
        self.register_buffer("w_lo", 1.0 - frac)
        self.register_buffer("w_hi", frac)

    def logp(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        f = x.squeeze(1)  # (B, N)
        f_at_events = self.w_lo * f[:, self.idx_lo] + self.w_hi * f[:, self.idx_lo + 1]
        event_term = f_at_events.sum(dim=-1)
        integral = self.dt * torch.exp(f).sum(dim=-1)
        return event_term - integral

docs.title: Log-Gaussian Cox process inference via GP flow matching¶
docs.text:
A log-Gaussian Cox process (LGCP) is an inhomogeneous Poisson process whose intensity \(\lambda(t) = e^{f(t)}\) has a GP prior on the log-intensity \(f\):

\[ f \sim \mathcal{GP}(\mu, k), \qquad \{t_i\} \mid f \sim \text{PoissonProcess}\bigl(e^{f}\bigr), \qquad \log p(\{t_i\} \mid f) = \sum_{i} f(t_i) - \int_0^T e^{f(t)}\, \mathrm{d}t. \]

We draw samples from the GP prior with a flow and guide them towards the posterior \(p(f \mid \{t_i\})\) using likelihood gradients. Two discretisations of the likelihood are compared: counting events per grid bin, and interpolating \(f\) at the exact event times.

docs.title: 1. Setup¶
docs.text: TRUE_* are the data-generating GP parameters, which we reuse for the prior; in practice they would be estimated from the data.

docs.title: 2. Simulated data¶
docs.text: Draw \(f^*\) from the GP on a fine grid and simulate events by Lewis–Shedler thinning: propose candidates from a homogeneous Poisson process at rate \(\lambda_{\max}\) and accept each at \(t\) with probability \(\lambda^*(t)/\lambda_{\max}\).

docs.title: 3. GP prior and sampler¶
docs.text: Both likelihoods share the same prior flow on an \(N\)-point grid. build_grid_in_box returns coordinates in \([0, 1)\), so the lengthscale is divided by \(T\).

docs.title: 4. Binned likelihood¶
docs.text:
Bin the events into the \(N\) grid cells. Cell \(j\) has count \(n_j\) and Poisson mean \(e^{f_j}\Delta t\):

\[ \log p(\{n_j\} \mid f) = \sum_{j} \bigl[ n_j f_j - e^{f_j} \Delta t \bigr]. \]

With \(N = 256\), the bin width \(\Delta t = T/N \approx 0.04\) is much shorter than the lengthscale of \(f\), so the binning error is small.

docs.title: 5. Exact likelihood (interpolated)¶
docs.text: Evaluate \(f\) at each event time \(t_i\) by linear interpolation of the grid values, and approximate \(\int_0^T e^{f(t)}\,\mathrm{d}t\) by a Riemann sum on the grid. The interpolation weights are precomputed, so logp is a cheap gather.

class MonotonicityCondition(BinaryCondition):
    """Non-decreasing, for a single-channel field on a 1D grid ordered left to right."""

    def smooth_eval_condition(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        f = x.squeeze(1)                           # (B, N)
        return (f[:, 1:] - f[:, :-1])[:, None, :]  # (B, 1, N-1)


class BoundedCondition(BinaryCondition):
    """Within [lower, upper] at each grid point, for a single-channel field."""

    def __init__(self, upper: Callable[[torch.Tensor], torch.Tensor],
                 lower: Callable[[torch.Tensor], torch.Tensor], grid: torch.Tensor,
                 v: float = 1e-6):
        super().__init__(v=v)
        self.register_buffer("upper_bound", upper(grid)[None, :])  # (1, N)
        self.register_buffer("lower_bound", lower(grid)[None, :])  # (1, N)

    def smooth_eval_condition(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        f = x.squeeze(1)  # (B, N)
        margins = [self.upper_bound - f, f - self.lower_bound]
        return torch.concat(margins, dim=-1)[:, None, :]  # (B, 1, 2N)

docs.title: Monotonic and Bounded GP Conditioning¶
docs.text:
This notebook conditions a GP regression posterior to satisfy two shape constraints at once: every sampled function must be non-decreasing, and must stay between a lower bound \(\ell(x) = 0\) and an upper bound \(u(x) = \frac{1}{3}\ln(30x + 1) + 0.1\). Such constraints are awkward to build into a GP analytically, but here they are just conditions applied while sampling the flow. The data are 7 exact observations of

\[f(x) = \frac{1}{3}\left[\arctan(20x - 10) - \arctan(-10)\right].\]

We compare several ways of imposing the constraints: gradient-based guidance with an ODE or SDE sampler, gradient-free Ensemble Kalman guidance, and pCN correction.

docs.title: 3. Target Function, Data and Bounds¶
docs.text: The 7 observations sit at \(x_i = 0.1 + 1/(i+1)\), \(i = 1, \dots, 7\), so they cluster in \([0.22, 0.6]\) and leave both ends of the domain to the prior and the constraints. plotter overlays the observations and the two bounds on the usual band-plus-traces figure.

docs.title: 4. GP Posterior¶
docs.text: An RBF kernel with lengthscale \(0.1\) and outputscale \(0.25\), set by hand rather than fitted. gp_posterior forms the conjugate posterior given the 7 observations; the flow evaluates its mean and kernel on the grid.

docs.title: 5. Unconditioned Samples¶
docs.text: Samples from the GP posterior alone interpolate the data but are free to decrease and to leave the bounds away from the observations.

docs.title: 6. Shape Conditions¶
docs.text: Both constraints are BinaryConditions: smooth_eval_condition returns margins that should be positive, and the base class scores them with \(\log\sigma(\text{margin}/v)\), a smooth relaxation of the hard constraint. Monotonicity uses the successive differences \(f(x_{j+1}) - f(x_j)\); boundedness uses \(u(x) - f(x)\) and \(f(x) - \ell(x)\). ProductCondition asks for both.

docs.title: 7. Conditioned Sampling¶
docs.text: The same condition can be imposed in several ways. Each subsection re-samples with it; all should give non-decreasing paths inside the bounds.

docs.title: 7.1 Gradient-based guidance (ODE)¶
docs.text: GuidanceMC estimates the guidance term by differentiating the condition through Monte-Carlo draws of the clean sample.

docs.title: 7.2 Gradient-based guidance (SDE)¶
docs.text: The same guidance, integrating the stochastic rather than the deterministic dynamics.

docs.title: 7.3 Gradient-free Ensemble Kalman guidance¶
docs.text: GuidanceEnsembleKalman estimates the guidance with an Ensemble Kalman Inversion update, so it never differentiates the condition.

docs.title: 7.4 Ensemble Kalman guidance with pCN correction¶
docs.text: Interleaving preconditioned Crank–Nicolson Metropolis steps corrects the remaining error in the guidance, allowing far fewer integration steps.

docs.title: 7.5 pCN correction alone¶
docs.text: With no guidance at all, the corrector does all the conditioning, using only condition.logp.

class PendulumCondition(EqualityCondition):
    """Damped pendulum ODE residual for a single-channel field on a uniform time grid."""

    def __init__(self, dt: float, sigma: float = 1.0, beta: float = 0.2):
        super().__init__(sigma=sigma)
        self.dt = float(dt)
        self.register_buffer("beta", torch.tensor(float(beta)))  # damping coefficient

    def residual(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        theta = x.squeeze(1)  # (B, N)
        # Centred differences at the interior points 1..N-2.
        dtheta_dt = (theta[:, 2:] - theta[:, :-2]) / (2 * self.dt)
        d2theta_dt2 = (theta[:, 2:] - 2 * theta[:, 1:-1] + theta[:, :-2]) / (self.dt * self.dt)
        residual = d2theta_dt2 + torch.sin(theta[:, 1:-1]) + self.beta * dtheta_dt
        return residual.unsqueeze(1)  # (B, 1, N-2)
class PendulumCondition(EqualityCondition): """Damped pendulum ODE residual for a single-channel field on a uniform time grid.""" def __init__(self, dt: float, sigma: float = 1.0, beta: float = 0.2): super().__init__(sigma=sigma) self.dt = float(dt) self.register_buffer("beta", torch.tensor(float(beta))) # damping coefficient def residual(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor: theta = x.squeeze(1) # (B, N) # Centred differences at the interior points 1..N-2. dtheta_dt = (theta[:, 2:] - theta[:, :-2]) / (2 * self.dt) d2theta_dt2 = (theta[:, 2:] - 2 * theta[:, 1:-1] + theta[:, :-2]) / (self.dt * self.dt) residual = d2theta_dt2 + torch.sin(theta[:, 1:-1]) + self.beta * dtheta_dt return residual.unsqueeze(1) # (B, 1, N-2) In [6]: Copied!

docs.title: Pendulum ODE Conditioning¶
docs.text:
This notebook fits a GP to noisy measurements of a damped pendulum's angle, then conditions its samples to obey the nonlinear pendulum ODE

\[\ddot{\theta} + \beta \dot{\theta} + \sin(\theta) = 0, \qquad \beta = 0.2.\]

The GP prior specifies only smoothness; the ODE, imposed through a finite-difference residual, adds the physics.

docs.title: 3. Data and GP Posterior¶
docs.text: The training data come from flow_inference/data/pendulum. The RBF kernel's lengthscale and outputscale are fitted to them by type-II maximum likelihood, and gp_posterior forms the conjugate posterior; the flow evaluates its mean and kernel on the grid.

docs.title: 4. Unconditioned Samples¶
docs.text: Samples from the GP posterior alone.

docs.title: 5. Conditioning on the Pendulum ODE¶
docs.text: PendulumCondition is an EqualityCondition with residual \(r = \ddot\theta + \beta\dot\theta + \sin\theta\), computed by centred differences at the interior grid points. Its log-likelihood is \(-\lVert r\rVert^2 / 2\sigma^2\), so \(\sigma\) sets how tightly the ODE is enforced.

class TimeEmbedding(nn.Module):
    """Fourier-feature embedding of t in [0, 1], followed by an MLP."""

    def __init__(self, dim: int):
        super().__init__()
        self.mlp = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(dim, dim), nn.SiLU(), nn.Linear(dim, dim))
        self.dim = dim

    def forward(self, t):
        freqs = torch.arange(1, self.dim // 2 + 1, device=t.device, dtype=t.dtype)
        angles = 2 * math.pi * t[:, None] * freqs[None, :]
        emb = torch.cat([torch.sin(angles), torch.cos(angles)], dim=-1)
        return self.mlp(emb)


class ConvBlock(nn.Module):
    """Two 3x3 convs with GroupNorm + SiLU and FiLM time conditioning in between."""

    def __init__(self, in_ch, out_ch, time_dim, gn_groups=8):
        super().__init__()
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(in_ch, out_ch, 3, padding=1)
        self.norm1 = nn.GroupNorm(gn_groups, out_ch)
        self.t_proj = nn.Linear(time_dim, out_ch * 2)
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(out_ch, out_ch, 3, padding=1)
        self.norm2 = nn.GroupNorm(gn_groups, out_ch)
        self.act = nn.SiLU()

    def forward(self, x, t_emb):
        h = self.act(self.norm1(self.conv1(x)))
        scale, shift = self.t_proj(t_emb)[:, :, None, None].chunk(2, dim=1)
        h = h * (1.0 + scale) + shift   # identity at scale = shift = 0
        h = self.act(self.norm2(self.conv2(h)))
        return h


class VectorFieldUNet(nn.Module):
    """Time-conditioned U-Net v_theta(x, t) with concat skips; `depth` halvings of the grid."""

    def __init__(self, in_ch=1, out_ch=1, base_ch=32, time_dim=64, depth=2, gn_groups=8):
        super().__init__()
        self.depth = depth
        self.time_mlp = TimeEmbedding(time_dim)

        chs = [base_ch * (2 ** i) for i in range(depth + 1)]  # e.g. depth=2 -> [C, 2C, 4C]

        self.enc_blocks = nn.ModuleList()
        self.enc_blocks.append(ConvBlock(in_ch, chs[0], time_dim, gn_groups))
        for i in range(depth):
            self.enc_blocks.append(ConvBlock(chs[i], chs[i + 1], time_dim, gn_groups))
        self.pool = nn.MaxPool2d(2)

        self.ups = nn.ModuleList()
        self.dec_blocks = nn.ModuleList()
        for i in reversed(range(depth)):
            self.ups.append(nn.Sequential(
                nn.Upsample(scale_factor=2, mode='bilinear', align_corners=False),
                nn.Conv2d(chs[i + 1], chs[i], 1),
            ))
            self.dec_blocks.append(ConvBlock(chs[i] * 2, chs[i], time_dim, gn_groups))

        self.out = nn.Conv2d(chs[0], out_ch, 1)

    def forward(self, x, t):
        t_emb = self.time_mlp(t)

        skips = []
        h = self.enc_blocks[0](x, t_emb)
        for i in range(self.depth):
            skips.append(h)
            h = self.enc_blocks[i + 1](self.pool(h), t_emb)

        for up, dec, skip in zip(self.ups, self.dec_blocks, reversed(skips)):
            h = dec(torch.cat([skip, up(h)], dim=1), t_emb)

        return self.out(h)

class RegionMassCondition(EqualityCondition):
    """Match the summed field within each of R regions to a target total."""

    def __init__(self, H, W, region_ids, region_targets, sigma=1e-2):
        super().__init__(sigma=sigma)
        self.H, self.W = H, W
        self.R = int(region_targets.numel())
        self.register_buffer("region_ids", region_ids.reshape(-1).long())     # (N,) in {0..R-1}
        self.register_buffer("region_targets", region_targets.reshape(-1))    # (R,)

    def residual(self, x):
        B = x.shape[0]
        x = x.reshape(B, -1)                                                   # (B, N)
        sums = torch.zeros(B, self.R, device=x.device, dtype=x.dtype)
        sums = sums.index_add(1, self.region_ids, x)                          # (B, R)
        return (sums - self.region_targets[None]).unsqueeze(1)                # (B, 1, R)

docs.title: Neural Flow: Conditioning a Learned Vector Field¶
docs.text: The other notebooks build the prior as a differentiable map from Gaussian increments to a field (GaussianIncrementFlow), but for many targets no such map exists and all we have are unconditional samples. Here we learn the prior instead: a time-conditioned U-Net velocity field \(v_\theta(x, t)\) is fitted by flow matching to samples of a Brown–Resnick max-stable field. Once wrapped in a NeuralFlow, the same EqualityCondition + GuidanceDPS posterior sampling works unchanged, which we show on an areal-disaggregation problem. A GPU is strongly recommended for training.

docs.title: 1. Training data¶
docs.text: Build the Brown–Resnick map and wrap it in a TrainingSampler, which pregenerates a pool of unconditional samples. These samples are all the neural flow ever sees of the target.

docs.title: 2. The vector field¶
docs.text: \(v_\theta(x, t)\) is a small U-Net acting on the field as a \(1 \times H \times W\) image, with Fourier time embeddings injected at every resolution by FiLM (per-channel scale and shift). Multiplicative time conditioning lets the network rescale the velocity across noise levels, which helps with heavy-tailed targets.

docs.title: 3. Train the flow¶
docs.text: Wrap the network in a NeuralFlow and fit it by flow matching, i.e. regressing the probability-flow ODE velocity on samples from the training pool.

docs.title: 4. Prior samples¶
docs.text: Integrate the learned flow with no guidance and check the samples look like the training data above.

docs.title: 5. Areal disaggregation¶
docs.text: Observe only the totals over 16 irregular regions (think census tracts or satellite footprints; here a Voronoi tessellation of random seed pixels) and recover a plausible fine-scale field. There is no closed-form map to draw a ground truth from, so it is a fresh draw from the training sampler.

class RegionMaxCondition(EqualityCondition):
    """Match the maximum of the field within each of R regions. Residual (length 2R):
      over-shoot: sum over each region of max(0, x - target_max)
      attainment: logsumexp_beta(x_region) / beta - target_max
    Larger beta gives a sharper surrogate and stiffer gradients.
    """

    def __init__(self, region_ids, region_maxes, beta=12.0, sigma=1e-2):
        super().__init__(sigma=sigma)
        self.R = int(region_maxes.numel())
        self.beta = beta
        self.register_buffer("region_ids", region_ids.reshape(-1).long())  # (N,) in {0..R-1}
        self.register_buffer("region_maxes", region_maxes.reshape(-1))  # (R,)

    def _region_softmax(self, x):
        # Per-region logsumexp / beta, stabilised by the per-region max.
        B = x.shape[0]
        ids = self.region_ids[None].expand(B, -1)  # (B, N)
        neg_inf = torch.full((B, self.R), float("-inf"), device=x.device, dtype=x.dtype)
        m = neg_inf.scatter_reduce(1, ids, x, reduce="amax", include_self=True)  # (B, R)
        m_pix = m.gather(1, ids)  # (B, N)
        z = torch.zeros(B, self.R, device=x.device, dtype=x.dtype)
        sumexp = z.scatter_add(1, ids, torch.exp(self.beta * (x - m_pix)))  # (B, R)
        return m + torch.log(sumexp) / self.beta  # (B, R)

    def residual(self, x):
        B = x.shape[0]
        x = x.reshape(B, -1)  # (B, N)
        tgt_pix = self.region_maxes[self.region_ids][None]  # (1, N)

        overshoot = torch.clamp(x - tgt_pix, min=0.0)  # (B, N)
        z = torch.zeros(B, self.R, device=x.device, dtype=x.dtype)
        over_r = z.scatter_add(1, self.region_ids[None].expand(B, -1), overshoot)  # (B, R)

        attain = self._region_softmax(x) - self.region_maxes[None]  # (B, R)
        return torch.cat([over_r, attain], dim=1).unsqueeze(1)  # (B, 1, 2R)

    condition = RegionMaxCondition(max_regions, region_maxes, beta=1000.0, sigma=1e-5).to(device)

class RegionMeanCondition(EqualityCondition):
    """Match the mean of the field within each of R regions."""

    def __init__(self, region_ids, region_means, sigma=1e-2):
        super().__init__(sigma=sigma)
        self.R = int(region_means.numel())
        ids = region_ids.reshape(-1).long()
        self.register_buffer("region_ids", ids)  # (N,) in {0..R-1}
        self.register_buffer("region_means", region_means.reshape(-1))  # (R,)
        counts = torch.zeros(self.R, device=ids.device).index_add(0, ids, torch.ones(ids.numel(), device=ids.device))
        self.register_buffer("counts", counts.clamp(min=1))  # (R,)

    def residual(self, x):
        B = x.shape[0]
        x = x.reshape(B, -1)  # (B, N)
        sums = torch.zeros(B, self.R, device=x.device, dtype=x.dtype).index_add(1, self.region_ids, x)
        return (sums / self.counts - self.region_means[None]).unsqueeze(1)  # (B, 1, R)

class CensoredObservationCondition(EqualityCondition):
    """Z(s_i) is known only to be below (left-censored) or above (right-censored) `limit`.
    Hinge residual, zero once the value is beyond the limit by `margin`:
      below: max(0, Z - (limit - margin))     above: max(0, (limit + margin) - Z)
    """

    def __init__(self, locations, below, limit=0.0, sigma=1e-2, margin=0.2):
        super().__init__(sigma=sigma)
        self.limit, self.margin = limit, margin
        self.register_buffer("locs", locations.long())  # (A,) flat indices
        self.register_buffer("below", below.bool())  # (A,)

    def residual(self, x):
        vals = x.reshape(x.shape[0], -1)[:, self.locs]  # (B, A)
        viol_below = torch.clamp(vals - (self.limit - self.margin), min=0.0)
        viol_above = torch.clamp((self.limit + self.margin) - vals, min=0.0)
        return torch.where(self.below[None, :], viol_below, viol_above).unsqueeze(1)  # (B, 1, A)


def censor_markers(below):
    return [
        {"flat_idx": censored_locs[~below], "marker": "+", "color": "red", "s": 40, "label": "above the limit (+)"},
        {"flat_idx": censored_locs[below], "marker": "_", "color": "deepskyblue", "s": 40, "label": "below the limit (-)"},
    ]

for name, flow in flows.items():
    truth = truths[name].reshape(-1)
    limit = truth.median().item()
    below = censored_below[name] = truth[censored_locs] < limit
    condition = CensoredObservationCondition(censored_locs, below, limit=limit, sigma=1e-5).to(device)
    post = results[name]["Censored observations"] = posterior_samples(flow, condition)

    signs_match = ((post.reshape(num_samples, -1)[:, censored_locs] < limit) == below[None]).double().mean().item()
    vmin, vmax = shared_range(truths[name], post)
    print(f"{name}: truth | posterior samples ({signs_match:.0%} of censored signs reproduced)")
    show(truths[name], titles=["ground truth"], markers=censor_markers(below), vmin=vmin, vmax=vmax)
    show(post, markers=censor_markers(below), vmin=vmin, vmax=vmax)

docs.title: Spatial Processes: Conditioning Non-Gaussian Random Fields¶
docs.text:
This notebook reproduces the spatial experiments of LatentFlow: A General Framework for Conditioning Stochastic Processes (Sharrock, Astfalck & Moss, 2026; Section 6.1, Figure 2 and Appendix G.2). Three spatial priors on an \(H \times W\) grid are each conditioned on four kinds of information:

Prior Character Gaussian process (Matérn-3/2, lengthscale 0.15) smooth, light tails Student-\(t\) process (\(\nu = 4\), Matérn-3/2, lengthscale 0.5) heavy tails, spatially coupled Cauchy convolution (lengthscale 0.05) very heavy tails, sharp local features Condition Data Sparse observations the field at 30 points Areal maxima the maximum over each of 8 irregular regions Areal means the mean over each of 20 irregular regions Censored observations at 60 points, only whether the field is above (\(+\)) or below (\(-\)) a detection limit

Every prior is the image of Gaussian innovations under a known map: the affine whitening map \(m + L\xi\) for the GP, and a non-linear map for the other two. Every condition is a likelihood on the field. The same guided flow handles all twelve combinations. Only two have a closed-form posterior: the linear conditions (sparse observations and areal means) under the GP.

docs.title: 1. Spatial priors¶
docs.text:
• Gaussian process: GaussianProcessFlow diffuses in the whitened space of the GP, so the generator is the affine map \(f = L\xi\) with \(LL^ op = K\).
  • Student-\(t\) process: a GP divided by a shared \(\sqrt{V/ u}\) with \(V \sim \chi^2_ u\), giving \(t_ u\) marginals (StudentTProcessMap).
  • Cauchy convolution: a Cauchy noise source convolved with a short-lengthscale kernel (CauchyConvolutionMap). Its infinite-variance source produces sharp, highly localised features.

The non-Gaussian priors are maps from Gaussian increments to a field, wrapped in a GaussianIncrementFlow. Each prior captures the kernel when it is built, so one kernel object is reused with a different lengthscale per prior.

docs.title: 2. Sampling helpers¶
docs.text: prior_samples integrates the probability-flow ODE with no guidance; posterior_samples adds Monte Carlo guidance from a condition and integrates the reverse SDE. Each demo below draws a ground-truth field from the prior, observes it, and draws posterior samples consistent with the observation. results collects every posterior for the summary figure.

docs.title: 3. Prior samples¶
docs.text: Unconditioned samples from each prior: the smooth Gaussian field, the Student-\(t\) field whose overall scale varies from draw to draw, and the Cauchy field with its isolated extreme spikes.

docs.title: 4. Observation layouts¶
docs.text: The sensor locations and regions are shared across priors, so the rows of the summary figure are directly comparable. Regions are Voronoi cells of random seed pixels.

docs.title: 5. Sparse observations¶
docs.text: Observe the field at 30 points and recover the whole field: kriging, but for any prior. PointObservation is an EqualityCondition on the observed pixels.

docs.title: 6. Areal maxima¶
docs.text: Each of 8 regions reports only its maximum (e.g. the peak pollutant reading in a monitoring zone): a non-linear operator that constrains the extreme of each region rather than its bulk. We encode it as two soft constraints per region: no pixel may exceed the reported maximum, and a smooth log-sum-exp surrogate of the region's maximum must attain it (the hard max has zero gradient away from the argmax).

docs.title: 7. Areal means¶
docs.text: Each of 20 regions reports only its mean (think census tracts or satellite footprints), and we recover a plausible fine-scale field. RegionMeanCondition is a linear operator, so under the GP prior alone this posterior is Gaussian; under the other two it is not.

docs.title: 8. Censored observations¶
docs.text: At 60 points we learn only whether the field is above (\(+\)) or below (\(-\)) a detection limit, as with a sensor that reports exceedance of a threshold but not the value. The limit is the median of the true field, so each prior gets a balanced mix of \(+\) and \(-\). The correct posterior integrates over the censored half-space rather than substituting the limit; a hinge residual that is zero once the value is beyond the limit by a margin encodes exactly this.

docs.title: 9. Summary¶
docs.text: One posterior sample per prior (rows) and condition (columns), as in Figure 2 of the LatentFlow paper. The samples respect each condition while keeping the character of their prior: smooth for the GP, globally rescaled for the Student-\(t\), spiky for the Cauchy field.

class PlumeMap(BaseMap):
    """Latent (B, 1, 6 + 2 * NUM_WIND_STEPS) -> concentration fields (B, 1, NUM_FRAMES * G * G)."""

    def __init__(self, wind_mean=(0.32, 0.14), theta=1.0, wind_sd=0.25, diffusivity=0.002, rate=0.03,
                 source_width=0.03, substeps=4):
        super().__init__(latent_dim=6 + 2 * NUM_WIND_STEPS, output_shape=(NUM_FRAMES, G, G), device=device)
        self.register_buffer("wind_mean", torch.tensor(wind_mean, device=device))
        self.theta, self.wind_sd, self.diffusivity, self.rate = theta, wind_sd, diffusivity, rate
        self.source_width, self.substeps = source_width, substeps

    def _map(self, z):
        B = z.shape[0]
        z = z[:, 0]
        dx = 1.0 / G
        x_src = 0.15 + 0.03 * z[:, 0]
        y_src = 0.45 + 0.08 * z[:, 1]
        rate = self.rate * torch.exp(0.3 * z[:, 2])
        wind = self.wind_mean[None] + 0.08 * z[:, 3:5]
        diffusivity = self.diffusivity * torch.exp(0.3 * z[:, 5])
        wind_noise = z[:, 6:].reshape(B, NUM_WIND_STEPS, 2)

        dist2 = (XX[None] - x_src[:, None, None]) ** 2 + (YY[None] - y_src[:, None, None]) ** 2
        source = torch.exp(-dist2 / (2 * self.source_width**2))
        source = source / source.mean(dim=(1, 2), keepdim=True)  # unit mass on the unit square
        emission = rate[:, None, None] * source
        diff = diffusivity[:, None, None]

        c = torch.zeros(B, G, G, device=z.device, dtype=z.dtype)
        frames = [c]
        h = DT / self.substeps
        for k in range(NUM_WIND_STEPS):
            w = 0.8 * torch.tanh(wind / 0.8)  # soft speed limit, for the CFL condition
            u, v = w[:, 0, None, None], w[:, 1, None, None]
            for _ in range(self.substeps):
                p = torch.nn.functional.pad(c, (1, 1, 1, 1))  # zero boundary
                left, right = p[:, 1:-1, :-2], p[:, 1:-1, 2:]
                up, down = p[:, :-2, 1:-1], p[:, 2:, 1:-1]  # up = larger y
                dc_dx = torch.where(u > 0, c - left, right - c) / dx
                dc_dy = torch.where(v > 0, c - down, up - c) / dx
                laplacian = (left + right + up + down - 4 * c) / dx**2
                c = c + h * (-u * dc_dx - v * dc_dy + diff * laplacian + emission)
            wind = wind + self.theta * (self.wind_mean[None] - wind) * DT + self.wind_sd * DT**0.5 * wind_noise[:, k]
            frames.append(c)
        return torch.stack(frames, dim=1).reshape(B, 1, -1)


flow = GaussianIncrementFlow(map=PlumeMap(), device=device)
sampler = IntegratorSampler(flow=flow)

def sample(condition=None):
    """`num_samples` fields (B, num_frames, G, G): the prior if `condition` is None, else guided."""
    guidance = None if condition is None else GuidanceMC(flow, condition).to(device)
    out = sampler.sample(num_samples, guidance=guidance, num_steps=NUM_STEPS).detach()
    return out.reshape(num_samples, NUM_FRAMES, G, G)

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(rows, len(SNAP_FRAMES), figsize=(1.7 * len(SNAP_FRAMES) + 1.6, 1.7 * rows),

    """(G, G) boolean mask of the pixels whose centres lie in a (x0, x1, y0, y1) box."""
    x0, x1, y0, y1 = box
    return (XX >= x0) & (XX <= x1) & (YY >= y0) & (YY <= y1)


def smooth_max(values, tau):

class SensorObservation(EqualityCondition):
    """Noisy point observations: the field at `pixels` in each of `frames` equals `observations`."""

    def __init__(self, frames, pixels, observations, sigma):
        super().__init__(sigma=sigma)
        self.register_buffer("frames", frames)
        self.register_buffer("pixels", pixels)
        self.register_buffer("observations", observations)  # (num_frames, num_pixels)

    def residual(self, x):
        fields = x.reshape(x.shape[0], NUM_FRAMES, -1)[:, self.frames][:, :, self.pixels]
        return (fields - self.observations[None]).reshape(x.shape[0], 1, -1)


sensor_samples = sample(SensorObservation(sensor_frames, sensors, observations, sigma=OBS_NOISE))

class BoxPeak(BinaryCondition):
    """Peak concentration in `box` over all times below `level` (above=False) or above it (above=True)."""

    def __init__(self, box, level, above, v=1e-3, smooth_tau=0.002):
        super().__init__(v=v)
        self.register_buffer("mask", box_mask(box).reshape(-1))
        self.level, self.sign, self.smooth_tau = level, 1.0 if above else -1.0, smooth_tau

    def smooth_eval_condition(self, x):
        inside = x.reshape(x.shape[0], NUM_FRAMES, -1)[:, :, self.mask].reshape(x.shape[0], -1)
        margin = self.sign * (smooth_max(inside, self.smooth_tau) - self.level)
        return margin[:, None, None]


def event_rate(condition, samples):
    return (condition.smooth_eval_condition(samples.reshape(samples.shape[0], 1, -1)) > 0).double().mean().item()


def prior_rate(condition, num=2000, chunk=400):
    """Event rate over `num` prior draws, simulated in chunks to bound memory."""
    hits = 0
    for _ in range(num // chunk):
        fields = flow.map(torch.randn(chunk, 1, flow.latent_dim, device=device))
        hits += (condition.smooth_eval_condition(fields) > 0).sum().item()
    return hits / num

docs.title: Advection–Diffusion Plume Conditioning¶
docs.text:
This notebook reproduces the advection–diffusion experiment of LatentFlow: A General Framework for Conditioning Stochastic Processes (Sharrock, Astfalck & Moss, 2026; Figures 5 and 17). A pollutant is released continuously from an uncertain source and carried by a randomly varying wind:

\[\partial_t c + \mathbf{w}(t)\cdot\nabla c = D\,\Delta c + q\,s(\mathbf{x}),\qquad d\mathbf{w} = \theta(\bar{\mathbf{w}} - \mathbf{w})\,dt + \sigma_w\,d\mathbf{W}_t,\]

on the unit square. The source position, release rate and diffusivity are random, and the wind is an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process. All of this randomness comes from just 160 Gaussian innovations: 6 for the source, initial wind and diffusivity, and 2 per time step for the wind. Guidance then conditions the plume on

  1. sparse sensors: noisy concentrations at 8 locations, observed at 4 times;
  2. obstacle avoidance: the concentration must stay below \(0.06\) in a central zone at all times;
  3. a detector hit: the peak concentration in a downstream detector must exceed \(0.40\), which fewer than 1% of prior plumes achieve.

docs.title: 1. Configuration¶
docs.text: A \(40 \times 40\) grid on the unit square and 77 wind steps up to \(t = 2.2\). Row 0 of every image is the top of the domain (\(y = 1\)).

docs.title: 2. The plume simulator¶
docs.text: PlumeMap is the generator \(T_\vartheta\). Each wind step is split into four first-order upwind substeps, which keeps the explicit scheme stable; a tanh soft-clamp bounds the wind speed. The domain has zero-concentration boundaries, so material is advected out of the box.

docs.title: 3. Helpers¶
docs.text: sample draws prior or guided fields, and plot_snapshots lays several regimes out as in the paper: two draws per regime, one row each, at six times.

docs.title: 4. Prior¶
docs.text: The plume's direction, spread and strength all vary from draw to draw.

docs.title: 5. Sparse sensors¶
docs.text: Take one prior plume as the "truth" and observe it at 8 sensors at 4 times, with noise of standard deviation \(0.02\). SensorObservation is an EqualityCondition whose sigma is that noise level.

docs.title: 6. Obstacle avoidance and detector hit¶
docs.text:
Both are binary events on the peak concentration in a box over the whole run, relaxed with a smooth maximum. BoxPeak returns a positive margin when the event holds: below a ceiling for the obstacle, above a floor for the detector.

The log-sum-exp maximum overestimates the true maximum by up to \(\tau \log n\), and here \(n\) is every pixel in the box at every time step (about 12,000). With \(\tau = 0.002\) that bias is below \(0.02\); a larger \(\tau\) would put the obstacle ceiling of \(0.06\) out of reach, and guidance would respond by switching the release off.

The mean wind blows straight at the obstacle, so avoiding it genuinely favours plumes that are deflected or weaker. A sharp relaxation (small v) over-weights the second route and leaves only a faint plume; the obstacle uses the softer v = 0.01.

PACEMAKER_2 = (25 / G, 29 / G, 25 / G, 29 / G)  # upper-right

def box_mask(box):
    """(G, G) boolean mask of the pixels whose centres lie in a (x0, x1, y0, y1) box."""
    x0, x1, y0, y1 = box
    return (XX >= x0) & (XX <= x1) & (YY >= y0) & (YY <= y1)


class FitzHughNagumoMap(BaseMap):
    """Latent (B, 1, NUM_FRAMES * G * G) -> activator fields (B, 1, NUM_FRAMES * G * G)."""

    def __init__(self, drive=0.25, sigma=0.35, background_noise=0.3, diffusion=0.6, eps=0.08, a=0.7, b=0.8,
                 speed=3.0, substeps=4):
        super().__init__(latent_dim=NUM_FRAMES * G * G, output_shape=(NUM_FRAMES, G, G), device=device)
        pacemakers = (box_mask(PACEMAKER_1) | box_mask(PACEMAKER_2)).double()
        self.register_buffer("drive", drive * pacemakers)
        self.register_buffer("noise_scale", sigma * (pacemakers + background_noise))
        self.diffusion, self.eps, self.a, self.b = diffusion, eps, a, b
        self.speed, self.substeps = speed, substeps

    def _map(self, z):
        B = z.shape[0]
        z = z.reshape(B, NUM_FRAMES, G, G)
        u = -1.2 + 0.05 * z[:, 0]  # near the resting state (u, v) = (-1.2, -0.62)
        v = torch.full_like(u, -0.62)
        frames = [u]
        h = self.speed * DT / self.substeps
        for k in range(1, NUM_FRAMES):
            for _ in range(self.substeps):
                p = torch.nn.functional.pad(u[:, None], (1, 1, 1, 1), mode="replicate")[:, 0]  # no-flux
                laplacian = p[:, :-2, 1:-1] + p[:, 2:, 1:-1] + p[:, 1:-1, :-2] + p[:, 1:-1, 2:] - 4 * u
                u, v = (u + h * (self.diffusion * laplacian + u - u**3 / 3 - v + self.drive),
                        v + h * self.eps * (u + self.a - self.b * v))
            u = u + self.noise_scale * (self.speed * DT) ** 0.5 * z[:, k]
            frames.append(u)
        return torch.stack(frames, dim=1).reshape(B, 1, -1)


flow = GaussianIncrementFlow(map=FitzHughNagumoMap(), device=device)
sampler = IntegratorSampler(flow=flow)
def box_mask(box): """(G, G) boolean mask of the pixels whose centres lie in a (x0, x1, y0, y1) box.""" x0, x1, y0, y1 = box return (XX >= x0) & (XX <= x1) & (YY >= y0) & (YY <= y1) class FitzHughNagumoMap(BaseMap): """Latent (B, 1, NUM_FRAMES * G * G) -> activator fields (B, 1, NUM_FRAMES * G * G).""" def __init__(self, drive=0.25, sigma=0.35, background_noise=0.3, diffusion=0.6, eps=0.08, a=0.7, b=0.8, speed=3.0, substeps=4): super().__init__(latent_dim=NUM_FRAMES * G * G, output_shape=(NUM_FRAMES, G, G), device=device) pacemakers = (box_mask(PACEMAKER_1) | box_mask(PACEMAKER_2)).double() self.register_buffer("drive", drive * pacemakers) self.register_buffer("noise_scale", sigma * (pacemakers + background_noise)) self.diffusion, self.eps, self.a, self.b = diffusion, eps, a, b self.speed, self.substeps = speed, substeps def _map(self, z): B = z.shape[0] z = z.reshape(B, NUM_FRAMES, G, G) u = -1.2 + 0.05 * z[:, 0] # near the resting state (u, v) = (-1.2, -0.62) v = torch.full_like(u, -0.62) frames = [u] h = self.speed * DT / self.substeps for k in range(1, NUM_FRAMES): for _ in range(self.substeps): p = torch.nn.functional.pad(u[:, None], (1, 1, 1, 1), mode="replicate")[:, 0] # no-flux laplacian = p[:, :-2, 1:-1] + p[:, 2:, 1:-1] + p[:, 1:-1, :-2] + p[:, 1:-1, 2:] - 4 * u u, v = (u + h * (self.diffusion * laplacian + u - u**3 / 3 - v + self.drive), v + h * self.eps * (u + self.a - self.b * v)) u = u + self.noise_scale * (self.speed * DT) ** 0.5 * z[:, k] frames.append(u) return torch.stack(frames, dim=1).reshape(B, 1, -1) flow = GaussianIncrementFlow(map=FitzHughNagumoMap(), device=device) sampler = IntegratorSampler(flow=flow) In [4]: Copied!

    draw_box(ax, PACEMAKER_1, "white"), draw_box(ax, PACEMAKER_2, "white")]);
prior_samples = sample() plot_snapshots([("Prior", prior_samples)], overlay=lambda ax, label, frame: [ draw_box(ax, PACEMAKER_1, "white"), draw_box(ax, PACEMAKER_2, "white")]); In [6]: Copied! 
class FiringPattern(BinaryCondition):
    def __init__(self, components, v=1e-3, smooth_tau=0.1, fire_level=0.5, silent_level=0.0):
        super().__init__(v=v)
        self.components = [(box_mask(box).double(), t0, t1, fires) for box, t0, t1, fires in components]
        self.smooth_tau, self.fire_level, self.silent_level = smooth_tau, fire_level, silent_level

    def smooth_eval_condition(self, x):
        u = x.reshape(x.shape[0], NUM_FRAMES, G, G)
        margins = []
        for mask, t0, t1, fires in self.components:
            activity = (u * mask).sum(dim=(-1, -2)) / mask.sum()  # (B, NUM_FRAMES)
            window = (times >= t0) & (times <= t1)
            peak = smooth_max(activity[:, window], self.smooth_tau)
            margins.append(peak - self.fire_level if fires else self.silent_level - peak)
        return torch.stack(margins, dim=-1)[:, None, :]


def event_rate(condition, samples):
    margins = condition.smooth_eval_condition(samples.reshape(samples.shape[0], 1, -1)).squeeze(1)
    return (margins.min(dim=-1).values > 0).double().mean().item()


patterns = {

docs.title: FitzHugh–Nagumo Excitable Medium Conditioning¶
docs.text:
This notebook reproduces the FitzHugh–Nagumo experiment of LatentFlow: A General Framework for Conditioning Stochastic Processes (Sharrock, Astfalck & Moss, 2026; Figures 5 and 18). An excitable medium follows the stochastic FitzHugh–Nagumo equations

\[\partial_t u = D\,\Delta u + u - \tfrac{1}{3}u^3 - v + I(\mathbf{x}) + \sigma(\mathbf{x})\,\xi(\mathbf{x}, t),\qquad \partial_t v = \varepsilon\,(u + a - b v),\]

where \(u\) is the activator, \(v\) the recovery variable and \(\xi\) space–time white noise. Two pacemaker patches (lower-left and upper-right) receive a sub-threshold drive \(I\) and extra noise, so in the prior each fires only sometimes, launching an activation front. The noise on a \(32 \times 32\) grid at 40 times gives about 41K Gaussian innovations. Guidance then conditions on the firing pattern:

  1. source 1 only: the lower-left pacemaker fires early (\(t \le 1.3\)) while the upper-right stays silent;
  2. source 2 only: the upper-right fires late (\(t \ge 1.8\), silent before) while the lower-left stays silent;
  3. both fire, in sequence: lower-left early, then upper-right late.

docs.title: 1. Configuration¶
docs.text: Grid units for space; the solver takes four Euler substeps per noise step for stability.

docs.title: 2. The excitable-medium simulator¶
docs.text: FitzHughNagumoMap is the generator \(T_\vartheta\): explicit Euler with no-flux boundaries. Time is rescaled by speed so that a firing and its front fit in the window. The noise is strongest at the pacemakers, which is what makes their firing random.

docs.title: 3. Helpers¶
docs.text: sample draws prior or guided fields, and plot_snapshots lays several regimes out as in the paper: two draws per regime, one row each, at six times.

docs.title: 4. Prior¶
docs.text: Each pacemaker fires in roughly 40% of prior draws, at a random time, and some draws stay quiet.

docs.title: 5. Firing conditions¶
docs.text: FiringPattern is a BinaryCondition built from components (pacemaker, t0, t1, fires). Each component takes the pacemaker-averaged activator, smooth-maximises it over the window \([t_0, t_1]\), and returns a margin that is positive when it crosses \(0.5\) (fires) or stays below \(0\) (silent).

docs.title: 6. Summary¶
docs.text: The four regimes as in Figure 18 of the paper. Green boxes mark pacemakers required to fire, red boxes those required to stay silent; a box turns green or red only once its requirement applies.

class AllenCahnMap(BaseMap):
    """Latent (B, 1, NUM_FRAMES * G * G) -> phase fields (B, 1, NUM_FRAMES * G * G)."""

    def __init__(self, eps=0.06, rate=5.0, sigma=0.6, init_scale=0.3):
        super().__init__(latent_dim=NUM_FRAMES * G * G, output_shape=(NUM_FRAMES, G, G), device=device)
        self.eps, self.rate, self.sigma, self.init_scale = eps, rate, sigma, init_scale

    def _map(self, z):
        B = z.shape[0]
        z = z.reshape(B, NUM_FRAMES, G, G)
        u = self.init_scale * z[:, 0]
        frames = [u]
        for k in range(1, NUM_FRAMES):
            laplacian = (u.roll(1, -1) + u.roll(-1, -1) + u.roll(1, -2) + u.roll(-1, -2) - 4 * u) / DX**2
            u = u + DT * (self.eps**2 * laplacian + self.rate * (u - u**3)) + self.sigma * DT**0.5 * z[:, k]
            frames.append(u)
        return torch.stack(frames, dim=1).reshape(B, 1, -1)


flow = GaussianIncrementFlow(map=AllenCahnMap(), device=device)
sampler = IntegratorSampler(flow=flow)
class AllenCahnMap(BaseMap): """Latent (B, 1, NUM_FRAMES * G * G) -> phase fields (B, 1, NUM_FRAMES * G * G).""" def __init__(self, eps=0.06, rate=5.0, sigma=0.6, init_scale=0.3): super().__init__(latent_dim=NUM_FRAMES * G * G, output_shape=(NUM_FRAMES, G, G), device=device) self.eps, self.rate, self.sigma, self.init_scale = eps, rate, sigma, init_scale def _map(self, z): B = z.shape[0] z = z.reshape(B, NUM_FRAMES, G, G) u = self.init_scale * z[:, 0] frames = [u] for k in range(1, NUM_FRAMES): laplacian = (u.roll(1, -1) + u.roll(-1, -1) + u.roll(1, -2) + u.roll(-1, -2) - 4 * u) / DX**2 u = u + DT * (self.eps**2 * laplacian + self.rate * (u - u**3)) + self.sigma * DT**0.5 * z[:, k] frames.append(u) return torch.stack(frames, dim=1).reshape(B, 1, -1) flow = GaussianIncrementFlow(map=AllenCahnMap(), device=device) sampler = IntegratorSampler(flow=flow) In [4]: Copied! 
def sample(condition=None):
    """`num_samples` fields (B, num_frames, G, G): the prior if `condition` is None, else guided."""
    guidance = None if condition is None else GuidanceMC(flow, condition).to(device)
    out = sampler.sample(num_samples, guidance=guidance, num_steps=NUM_STEPS).detach()
    return out.reshape(num_samples, NUM_FRAMES, G, G)

    `regimes` is a list of (label, samples); `overlay(ax, label, frame)` draws a regime's
    condition on a panel.

    rows = len(regimes) * draws
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(rows, len(SNAP_FRAMES), figsize=(1.7 * len(SNAP_FRAMES) + 1.6, 1.7 * rows),
                             squeeze=False)
    for r, (label, samples) in enumerate(regimes):
        for d in range(draws):
            row = r * draws + d
            for col, frame in enumerate(SNAP_FRAMES):
                ax = axes[row, col]
                im = ax.imshow(samples[d, frame].cpu(), cmap=CMAP, vmin=VMIN, vmax=VMAX)
                ax.set_xticks([])

class SensorObservation(EqualityCondition):
    """Noisy point observations: the field at `pixels` in each of `frames` equals `observations`."""

    def __init__(self, frames, pixels, observations, sigma):

        self.register_buffer("frames", frames)
        self.register_buffer("pixels", pixels)
        self.register_buffer("observations", observations)  # (num_frames, num_pixels)

    def residual(self, x):
        fields = x.reshape(x.shape[0], NUM_FRAMES, -1)[:, self.frames][:, :, self.pixels]
        return (fields - self.observations[None]).reshape(x.shape[0], 1, -1)

class FinalRegionMeans(EqualityCondition):
    """The final field's mean over each of R masks equals the matching target."""

    def __init__(self, masks, targets, sigma=1e-3):
        super().__init__(sigma=sigma)
        weights = masks.double()
        self.register_buffer("weights", weights / weights.sum(dim=(1, 2), keepdim=True))  # (R, G, G)
        self.register_buffer("targets", torch.as_tensor(targets, device=masks.device, dtype=weights.dtype))

    def residual(self, x):
        final = x.reshape(x.shape[0], NUM_FRAMES, G, G)[:, -1]
        means = torch.einsum("bij,rij->br", final, self.weights)
        return (means - self.targets[None])[:, None, :]

        [0.4, -0.4, -0.4, 0.4],
    ),
    "Annular ring": (
        torch.stack([RADIUS < 0.3, (RADIUS >= 0.3) & (RADIUS <= 0.65), RADIUS > 0.65]),
        [-0.5, 0.5, -0.5],
    ),
    "Phase front": (
        torch.stack([XX < -0.3, XX.abs() <= 0.3, XX > 0.3]),

}

docs.title: Stochastic Allen–Cahn Phase-Field Conditioning¶
docs.text:
This notebook reproduces the Allen–Cahn experiment of LatentFlow: A General Framework for Conditioning Stochastic Processes (Sharrock, Astfalck & Moss, 2026; Figures 5 and 19). A phase field on \([-1, 1]^2\) follows the stochastic Allen–Cahn equation

\[\partial_t u = \epsilon^2 \Delta u + \kappa\,(u - u^3) + \sigma\,\xi(\mathbf{x}, t),\]

with periodic boundaries, starting from small random noise. The double-well reaction drives \(u\) towards the phases \(\pm 1\), giving stochastic domain coarsening. The initial field and the noise on a \(64 \times 64\) grid at 30 times give 122,880 Gaussian innovations. Guidance then conditions on

  1. sparse sensors: noisy point observations at 36 locations, at each of 6 times;
  2. quadrant means: the final field's mean in each quadrant is \((+0.1, -0.1, -0.1, +0.1)\), a checkerboard;
  3. an annular ring: positive mean (\(+0.3\)) in the annulus \(0.30 \le r \le 0.65\), negative (\(-0.3\)) in the core and exterior;
  4. a phase front: means \((-0.2, 0, +0.2)\) in three vertical strips with boundaries at \(|x| = 0.3\).

Conditions 2–4 constrain only statistics of the final field; the earlier frames follow from the dynamics.

docs.title: 2. The Allen–Cahn simulator¶
docs.text: AllenCahnMap is the generator \(T_\vartheta\): explicit Euler–Maruyama with a periodic five-point Laplacian. The first latent slice sets the initial field and each later slice is one step's noise.

docs.title: 3. Helpers¶
docs.text: sample draws prior or guided fields, and plot_snapshots lays several regimes out as in the paper: two draws per regime, one row each, at six times.

docs.title: 4. Prior¶
docs.text: Small random initial noise coarsens into \(\pm 1\) domains at random positions.

docs.title: 5. Sparse sensors¶
docs.text: Take one prior field as the "truth" and observe it on a \(6 \times 6\) grid of sensors at each snapshot time, with noise of standard deviation \(0.05\). SensorObservation is an EqualityCondition whose sigma is that noise level.

docs.title: 6. Region means of the final field¶
docs.text: FinalRegionMeans is an EqualityCondition on the final frame: the mean over each region (a boolean mask) must equal its target. One class covers all three layouts.

docs.title: 7. Summary¶
docs.text: The five regimes as in Figure 19 of the paper. Region outlines and target signs are drawn on the final frame, which is the only one constrained.

def price_index(samples):
    """(B, 2, num_times) samples -> (B, num_times) price index 100 exp(X_t)."""
    return 100.0 * torch.exp(samples[:, 0, :])


def plot_paths(ax, samples, title, labels=True):
    """The first NUM_PLOTTED samples' volatility on `ax` (left) and price index on a twin axis
    (right), as in the paper. Returns the twin."""
    price_ax = ax.twinx()
    ax.set_zorder(price_ax.get_zorder() + 1)  # volatility, legend and event box above the prices
    ax.patch.set_visible(False)
    count = min(samples.shape[0], NUM_PLOTTED)
    plot_traces(samples[:, 1], x=times, color=COLORS["volatility"], count=count, alpha=0.45, linewidth=1.1, ax=ax)
    plot_traces(price_index(samples), x=times, color=COLORS["price index"], count=count, alpha=0.45, linewidth=1.1,
                ax=price_ax)
    ax.set_title(title, pad=8)
    ax.set_xlabel("time")
    ax.set_ylim(0.0, 0.75)
    price_ax.set_ylim(65, 125)
    if labels:
        ax.set_ylabel("volatility", color=COLORS["volatility"])
        price_ax.set_ylabel("price index", color=COLORS["price index"])
    ax.grid(True, color="#e5e7eb", linewidth=0.8)
    ax.margins(x=0.01)
    return price_ax


def channel_legend(ax, loc):
    handles = [Line2D([], [], color=COLORS[name], linewidth=2.0, label=name) for name in CHANNELS]
    ax.legend(handles=handles, loc=loc)


def show_event(ax, price_ax, loc):
    threshold_lines({"price index": price_ax, "volatility": ax})
    event_box(ax, loc)


def plot_observations(ax, observations, channels, mask, transform=lambda y: y):
    """Observed values as black dots."""
    for channel in channels:
        ax.scatter(as_numpy(times[mask]), as_numpy(transform(observations[channel, mask])),
                   color="black", edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.6, s=30, zorder=5)


def event_box(ax, loc):
    """The event's components as coloured lines of text in a white box, as in the paper."""
    lines = [TextArea(line["text"], textprops=dict(color=line["color"], fontsize=9)) for line in EVENT_LINES]
    box = AnchoredOffsetbox(loc=loc, child=VPacker(children=lines, align="left", pad=0, sep=2),

    box.patch.set_edgecolor("#9ca3af")

def threshold_lines(axes_by_channel):
    """A dashed line at every event threshold: across the whole path for extremes, over the
    final stretch for terminal conditions."""
    for line in EVENT_LINES:
        xmin = 0.0 if line["span"] == "path" else 0.85
        axes_by_channel[line["channel"]].axhline(line["y"], xmin=xmin, color=line["color"],

def smooth_max(values: torch.Tensor, tau: float) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Log-sum-exp maximum over time: differentiable, and within tau * log(num_times) of the hard max."""
    return tau * torch.logsumexp(values / tau, dim=-1)


def smooth_min(values: torch.Tensor, tau: float) -> torch.Tensor:
    return -smooth_max(-values, tau)


def event_rate(condition: BinaryCondition, samples: torch.Tensor) -> float:
    """Fraction of samples meeting every component of the event (all margins > 0)."""
    margins = condition.smooth_eval_condition(samples).squeeze(1)  # (B, components)

class HestonMap(BaseMap):
    """Coupled (log-price, volatility) Euler-Maruyama simulator for the Heston model."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        num_times: int,
        mu: float = 0.05,
        kappa: float = 3.0,
        theta: float = 0.04,
        xi: float = 0.55,
        rho: float = -0.65,
    ):
        super().__init__(
            latent_dim=num_times,
            output_shape=(num_times,),
            channels=2,
            device=device,
            dtype=torch.float64,
        )
        self.num_times = num_times
        self.dt = horizon / (num_times - 1)
        self.sqrt_dt = self.dt ** 0.5
        self.mu = mu
        self.kappa = kappa
        self.theta = theta
        self.xi = xi
        self.rho = rho

    def _map(self, z: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """z: (B, 2, num_times) iid N(0, 1) -> (B, 2, num_times) (log-price, volatility) paths."""
        B, C, N = z.shape
        if C != 2 or N != self.num_times:
            raise ValueError(f"expected latent shape (B, 2, {self.num_times}), got {tuple(z.shape)}")

        log_price = 0.015 * z[:, 0, 0]
        variance = (0.04 + 0.010 * z[:, 1, 0]).clamp(0.006, 0.25)
        log_price_path = [log_price]
        volatility_path = [variance.sqrt()]

        for k in range(self.num_times - 1):
            variance_pos = variance.clamp_min(1e-5)
            dW_variance = self.sqrt_dt * z[:, 1, k + 1]
            dW_price = self.rho * dW_variance + (1.0 - self.rho**2) ** 0.5 * self.sqrt_dt * z[:, 0, k + 1]

            log_price = log_price + (self.mu - 0.5 * variance_pos) * self.dt + variance_pos.sqrt() * dW_price
            variance = variance + self.kappa * (self.theta - variance_pos) * self.dt + self.xi * variance_pos.sqrt() * dW_variance
            variance = variance.clamp(1e-5, 0.80)
            log_price = 0.75 * torch.tanh(log_price / 0.75)

            log_price_path.append(log_price)
            volatility_path.append(variance.sqrt())

        return torch.stack(
            [torch.stack(log_price_path, dim=-1), torch.stack(volatility_path, dim=-1)],
            dim=1,
        )  # (B, 2, num_times)

class NoisyObservation(EqualityCondition):
    """Gaussian observations of `channels` at the masked times, with noise standard deviation `sigma`."""

    def __init__(self, observations: torch.Tensor, channels: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor, sigma: float):
        super().__init__(sigma=sigma)
        self.register_buffer("observations", observations)
        self.register_buffer("channels", channels)
        self.register_buffer("mask", mask)

    def residual(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        selected = x[:, self.channels][:, :, self.mask]
        target = self.observations[self.channels][:, self.mask]
        return selected - target[None, :, :]

class MarketShock(BinaryCondition):
    """Minimum price index below `min_price` and maximum volatility above `max_vol`."""

    def __init__(self, min_price: float, max_vol: float, v: float = 1e-5, smooth_tau: float = 0.025):
        super().__init__(v=v)
        self.log_min_price = torch.log(torch.tensor(min_price / 100.0)).item()
        self.max_vol = max_vol
        self.smooth_tau = smooth_tau

    def smooth_eval_condition(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        log_price = x[:, 0, :]
        volatility = x[:, 1, :]
        components = torch.stack(
            [
                self.log_min_price - smooth_min(log_price, self.smooth_tau),
                smooth_max(volatility, self.smooth_tau) - self.max_vol,
            ],
            dim=-1,
        )
        return components[:, None, :]  # (B, 1, 2)

docs.title: Heston Stochastic-Volatility Conditioning¶
docs.text:
This notebook reproduces the Heston row of Figure 4 in LatentFlow: A General Framework for Conditioning Stochastic Processes (Sharrock, Astfalck & Moss, 2026). A stochastic-volatility process is written as the deterministic image of Gaussian innovations, pushed through an Euler–Maruyama simulator of the log-price \(X_t\) and instantaneous variance \(V_t\):

\[dX_t = \left(\mu - \tfrac{1}{2} V_t\right)dt + \sqrt{V_t}\,dW^X_t, \qquad dV_t = \kappa(\theta - V_t)\,dt + \xi\sqrt{V_t}\,dW^V_t,\]

with leverage correlation \(\mathrm{corr}(dW^X_t, dW^V_t) = \rho < 0\). The price index is \(100\,e^{X_t}\). Guidance then conditions the paths on

  1. data: noisy observations of the price over the early window \(t \le 0.2\);
  2. an event: a market shock, where the price falls below \(87\) at some point and volatility spikes above \(0.42\);
  3. both at once.

Volatility is never observed directly, so conditioning on prices alone must infer it.

docs.title: 2. Configuration¶
docs.text: One trading year discretised into \(N = 126\) steps; the grid is defined at module level so the map and the conditions can both read it. The second cell holds the plotting and event-rate helpers reused by every figure. Price and volatility live on different scales, so each panel puts the price index on a twin axis, as in the paper.

docs.title: 3. The Heston SDE¶
docs.text: HestonMap is the generator \(T_\vartheta\): it integrates the correlated two-factor Heston model with Euler–Maruyama. Log-price and volatility are coupled channels of one asset, so the map consumes the whole (B, 2, num_times) latent tensor: the first time slice perturbs the initial state and the rest supply the Brownian increments, correlated through \(\rho\). The variance mean-reverts to \(\theta\) at speed \(\kappa\) with volatility-of-volatility \(\xi\); clamps and a tanh soft-clamp on the log-price keep the paths bounded.

docs.title: 4. Prior¶
docs.text: GaussianIncrementFlow runs the flow over the iid Gaussian increments and pushes them through the map, so sampling it without guidance gives unconditioned prior paths.

docs.title: 5. Conditioned on Data¶
docs.text: Take one prior path as the "truth" and observe only its price at every third trading day of the early window \(t \le 0.2\), with log-price noise of standard deviation \(0.005\). NoisyObservation is an EqualityCondition on the log-price channel whose sigma is that noise level. The observations fix the early price; the volatility they imply is inferred, not observed.

docs.title: 6. Conditioned on an Event¶
docs.text: Now condition on the market shock alone: the price index drops below \(87\) at some point in the year and volatility spikes above \(0.42\). MarketShock is a BinaryCondition with one margin per component, using smooth (log-sum-exp) extremes over time; the price threshold is applied on the log scale, \(\min_t X_t < \log 0.87\). Guidance must satisfy both at once.

docs.title: 7. Conditioned on Both¶
docs.text: ProductCondition multiplies the two likelihoods, so guidance must follow the observed early prices and produce the shock later in the year.

docs.title: 8. Summary¶
docs.text: The four regimes side by side, as in Figure 4 of the LatentFlow paper. The same prior, flow and sampler are used throughout; only the condition changes.
