def threshold_lines(axes_by_channel):
    """A dashed line at every event threshold: across the whole path for extremes, over the
    final stretch for terminal conditions."""
    for line in EVENT_LINES:
        xmin = 0.0 if line["span"] == "path" else 0.85
        axes_by_channel[line["channel"]].axhline(line["y"], xmin=xmin, color=line["color"],
                                                 linestyle="--", linewidth=1.5, zorder=4)


def smooth_max(values: torch.Tensor, tau: float) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Log-sum-exp maximum over time: differentiable, and within tau * log(num_times) of the hard max."""
    return tau * torch.logsumexp(values / tau, dim=-1)


def smooth_min(values: torch.Tensor, tau: float) -> torch.Tensor:
    return -smooth_max(-values, tau)


def event_rate(condition: BinaryCondition, samples: torch.Tensor) -> float:
    """Fraction of samples meeting every component of the event (all margins > 0)."""
    margins = condition.smooth_eval_condition(samples).squeeze(1)  # (B, components)
    return (margins.min(dim=-1).values > 0).double().mean().item()

class LotkaVolterraMap(BaseMap):
    """Coupled (prey, predator) Euler-Maruyama simulator in log-space."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        num_times: int,
        alpha: float = 1.10,
        beta: float = 0.45,
        delta: float = 0.35,
        gamma: float = 0.75,
        sigma: float = 0.08,
    ):
        super().__init__(
            latent_dim=num_times,
            output_shape=(num_times,),
            channels=2,
            device=device,
            dtype=torch.float64,
        )
        self.num_times = num_times
        self.alpha = alpha
        self.beta = beta
        self.delta = delta
        self.gamma = gamma
        self.sigma = sigma

    def _map(self, z: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """z: (B, 2, num_times) iid N(0, 1) -> (B, 2, num_times) (prey, predator) paths."""
        B, C, N = z.shape
        if C != 2 or N != self.num_times:
            raise ValueError(f"expected latent shape (B, 2, {self.num_times}), got {tuple(z.shape)}")

        sigma = self.sigma
        sqrt_dt = dt ** 0.5

        log_prey = torch.log(torch.full((B,), 2.0, device=z.device, dtype=z.dtype)) + 0.15 * z[:, 0, 0]
        log_predator = torch.log(torch.full((B,), 1.0, device=z.device, dtype=z.dtype)) + 0.15 * z[:, 1, 0]
        prey_path = [log_prey.exp()]
        predator_path = [log_predator.exp()]

        for k in range(self.num_times - 1):
            prey = log_prey.exp()
            predator = log_predator.exp()
            log_prey = log_prey + (self.alpha - self.beta * predator - 0.5 * sigma**2) * dt + sigma * sqrt_dt * z[:, 0, k + 1]
            log_predator = log_predator + (self.delta * prey - self.gamma - 0.5 * sigma**2) * dt + sigma * sqrt_dt * z[:, 1, k + 1]
            prey_path.append(log_prey.exp())
            predator_path.append(log_predator.exp())

        return torch.stack([torch.stack(prey_path, dim=-1), torch.stack(predator_path, dim=-1)], dim=1)

class NoisyObservation(EqualityCondition):
    """Gaussian observations of `channels` at the masked times, with noise standard deviation `sigma`."""

    def __init__(self, observations: torch.Tensor, channels: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor, sigma: float):
        super().__init__(sigma=sigma)
        self.register_buffer("observations", observations)
        self.register_buffer("channels", channels)
        self.register_buffer("mask", mask)

    def residual(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        selected = x[:, self.channels][:, :, self.mask]
        target = self.observations[self.channels][:, self.mask]
        return selected - target[None, :, :]

class PreyBoom(BinaryCondition):
    """Peak prey above `threshold`."""

    def __init__(self, threshold: float, v: float = 0.01, smooth_tau: float = 0.05):
        super().__init__(v=v)
        self.threshold = threshold
        self.smooth_tau = smooth_tau

    def smooth_eval_condition(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        margin = smooth_max(x[:, 0, :], self.smooth_tau) - self.threshold  # (B,)
        return margin[:, None, None]  # (B, 1, 1)

docs.title: Stochastic Lotka–Volterra Conditioning¶
docs.text:
This notebook reproduces the Lotka–Volterra row of Figure 4 in LatentFlow: A General Framework for Conditioning Stochastic Processes (Sharrock, Astfalck & Moss, 2026). A stochastic predator–prey process is written as the deterministic image of Gaussian innovations: the increments are pushed through an Euler–Maruyama simulator of

\[d\log u = \left(\alpha - \beta v - \tfrac{1}{2}\sigma^2\right)dt + \sigma\,dW_u,\qquad d\log v = \left(\delta u - \gamma - \tfrac{1}{2}\sigma^2\right)dt + \sigma\,dW_v,\]

where \(u\) is the prey and \(v\) the predator population. Guidance then conditions the paths on

  1. data: dense, noisy observations of both species over an early window \(t \le 1.25\);
  2. an event: a prey boom, peak prey \(> 7\), which the prior reaches only rarely;
  3. both at once.

The two species are coupled through the dynamics, so a condition on prey alone also reshapes the predator.

docs.title: 2. Configuration¶
docs.text: The time grid is defined at module level so the map and the conditions can both read it. The second cell holds the plotting and event-rate helpers reused by every figure.

docs.title: 3. The Stochastic Lotka–Volterra SDE¶
docs.text: LotkaVolterraMap is the generator \(T_\vartheta\): it integrates the SDE above in log-space with Euler–Maruyama. Prey and predator are coupled channels of one system, so the map consumes the whole (B, 2, num_times) latent tensor: the first time slice perturbs the initial populations and the rest supply the Brownian increments.

docs.title: 4. Prior¶
docs.text: GaussianIncrementFlow runs the flow over the iid Gaussian increments and pushes them through the map, so sampling it without guidance gives unconditioned prior paths.

docs.title: 5. Conditioned on Data¶
docs.text: Take one prior path as the "truth" and observe both populations at every other time point of the early window \(t \le 1.25\), with Gaussian noise of standard deviation \(0.05\). NoisyObservation is an EqualityCondition whose sigma is that noise level, so its log-likelihood is the observation model itself. The data pin down the first oscillation; the spread of the posterior grows again after the window.

docs.title: 6. Conditioned on an Event¶
docs.text:
Now condition on a qualitative event with no data at all: a prey boom, with the prey population peaking above \(7\). PreyBoom is a BinaryCondition whose margin is a smooth (log-sum-exp) maximum of the prey path minus the threshold, positive when the event holds. Only a couple of percent of prior paths reach it.

The temperature v sets how sharp the relaxation is. A very small v makes the guidance push hard until the margin is clearly positive, so it overshoots into implausibly large booms; too large a v lets the data outweigh the event once both are imposed. v = 0.01 balances the two.

docs.title: 7. Conditioned on Both¶
docs.text: ProductCondition multiplies the two likelihoods, so guidance must fit the early observations and produce a later prey boom. The posterior keeps the observed start and bends the subsequent dynamics towards the event.

docs.title: 8. Summary¶
docs.text: The four regimes side by side, as in Figure 4 of the LatentFlow paper. The same prior, flow and sampler are used throughout; only the condition changes.

def double_well_potential(xy: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Paper Eq. 46 potential. xy: (..., 2) -> (...,) energy."""
    x, y = xy[..., 0], xy[..., 1]
    term_1 = 4.0 * (1.0 - x**2 - y**2) ** 2
    term_2 = 2.0 * (x**2 - 2.0) ** 2
    term_3 = ((x + y) ** 2 - 1.0) ** 2
    term_4 = ((x - y) ** 2 - 1.0) ** 2
    return (term_1 + term_2 + term_3 + term_4 - 2.0) / 6.0


def double_well_force(xy: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Analytic force -grad U. xy: (..., 2) -> (..., 2)."""
    x, y = xy[..., 0], xy[..., 1]
    a = 1.0 - x**2 - y**2
    b = x**2 - 2.0
    c = (x + y) ** 2 - 1.0
    d = (x - y) ** 2 - 1.0
    grad_x = (-16.0 * a * x + 8.0 * b * x + 4.0 * c * (x + y) + 4.0 * d * (x - y)) / 6.0
    grad_y = (-16.0 * a * y + 4.0 * c * (x + y) - 4.0 * d * (x - y)) / 6.0
    return -torch.stack([grad_x, grad_y], dim=-1)


def double_well_step_fn(xy: torch.Tensor, noise: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """One Euler-Maruyama step of dR = -grad U dt + sqrt(2 kB lambda) dW."""
    return xy + double_well_force(xy) * dt_md + noise_std * noise


class DoubleWellDualChannelMap(BaseMap):
    """Coupled (x, y) Euler-Maruyama simulator launched from R_A."""

    def __init__(self, num_steps: int = num_md_steps):
        super().__init__(
            latent_dim=num_steps,
            output_shape=(num_steps + 1,),
            channels=2,
            device=device,
            dtype=torch.float64,
        )
        self.num_steps = num_steps
        self.register_buffer("R_A", R_A.clone())

    def _map(self, z: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """z: (B, 2, num_steps) iid N(0, 1) -> (B, 2, num_steps + 1) (x, y) paths."""
        B, C, L = z.shape
        if C != 2 or L != self.num_steps:
            raise ValueError(f"expected latent shape (B, 2, {self.num_steps}), got {tuple(z.shape)}")
        noises = z.permute(0, 2, 1)  # (B, num_steps, 2)
        xy = self.R_A[None, :].expand(B, 2)
        path = [xy]
        for k in range(self.num_steps):
            xy = double_well_step_fn(xy, noises[:, k])
            path.append(xy)
        return torch.stack(path, dim=-1)  # (B, 2, num_steps + 1)
def double_well_potential(xy: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor: """Paper Eq. 46 potential. xy: (..., 2) -> (...,) energy.""" x, y = xy[..., 0], xy[..., 1] term_1 = 4.0 * (1.0 - x**2 - y**2) ** 2 term_2 = 2.0 * (x**2 - 2.0) ** 2 term_3 = ((x + y) ** 2 - 1.0) ** 2 term_4 = ((x - y) ** 2 - 1.0) ** 2 return (term_1 + term_2 + term_3 + term_4 - 2.0) / 6.0 def double_well_force(xy: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor: """Analytic force -grad U. xy: (..., 2) -> (..., 2).""" x, y = xy[..., 0], xy[..., 1] a = 1.0 - x**2 - y**2 b = x**2 - 2.0 c = (x + y) ** 2 - 1.0 d = (x - y) ** 2 - 1.0 grad_x = (-16.0 * a * x + 8.0 * b * x + 4.0 * c * (x + y) + 4.0 * d * (x - y)) / 6.0 grad_y = (-16.0 * a * y + 4.0 * c * (x + y) - 4.0 * d * (x - y)) / 6.0 return -torch.stack([grad_x, grad_y], dim=-1) def double_well_step_fn(xy: torch.Tensor, noise: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor: """One Euler-Maruyama step of dR = -grad U dt + sqrt(2 kB lambda) dW.""" return xy + double_well_force(xy) * dt_md + noise_std * noise class DoubleWellDualChannelMap(BaseMap): """Coupled (x, y) Euler-Maruyama simulator launched from R_A.""" def __init__(self, num_steps: int = num_md_steps): super().__init__( latent_dim=num_steps, output_shape=(num_steps + 1,), channels=2, device=device, dtype=torch.float64, ) self.num_steps = num_steps self.register_buffer("R_A", R_A.clone()) def _map(self, z: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor: """z: (B, 2, num_steps) iid N(0, 1) -> (B, 2, num_steps + 1) (x, y) paths.""" B, C, L = z.shape if C != 2 or L != self.num_steps: raise ValueError(f"expected latent shape (B, 2, {self.num_steps}), got {tuple(z.shape)}") noises = z.permute(0, 2, 1) # (B, num_steps, 2) xy = self.R_A[None, :].expand(B, 2) path = [xy] for k in range(self.num_steps): xy = double_well_step_fn(xy, noises[:, k]) path.append(xy) return torch.stack(path, dim=-1) # (B, 2, num_steps + 1) In [4]: Copied! 
def plot_on_landscape(samples, num_paths=64, title=None):
    """Draw (B, 2, L) paths over filled contours of U (cf. paper Figure 4, top row)."""
    xy = samples.detach().cpu().numpy()
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 6))
    X, Y = np.meshgrid(np.linspace(-1.5, 1.5, 300), np.linspace(-1.5, 1.5, 300))
    Z = double_well_potential(torch.from_numpy(np.stack([X, Y], -1))).numpy()
    ax.contourf(X, Y, Z, levels=100, vmax=3, zorder=0)
    cmap = plt.get_cmap("gist_rainbow")
    for i in range(min(num_paths, xy.shape[0])):
        ax.plot(xy[i, 0], xy[i, 1], color=cmap(i / num_paths), lw=0.6, alpha=0.6, zorder=1)
    ax.scatter([-1.118, 1.118], [0.0, 0.0], c="w", edgecolors="k", s=300, zorder=3)  # wells A, B
    ax.scatter([0.0, 0.0], [1.0, -1.0], c="w", edgecolors="k", marker="*", s=400, zorder=3)  # saddles
    ax.set_xlim(-1.5, 1.5)
    ax.set_ylim(-1.5, 1.5)
    ax.set_xlabel("x")
    ax.set_ylabel("y")
    if title:
        ax.set_title(title)
    plt.tight_layout()
    return ax


def transition_path_metrics(samples):
    """THP, RMSD and ETS, each read at the path's closest approach to R_B."""
    path = samples.permute(0, 2, 1)  # (B, L, 2)
    dist = torch.linalg.norm(path - R_B[None, None, :], dim=-1)  # (B, L)
    rmsd, hit_idx = dist.min(dim=-1)  # closest approach
    hit = rmsd < 0.5
    energy = double_well_potential(path)  # (B, L)
    steps = torch.arange(path.shape[1], device=samples.device)[None, :]
    ets = energy.masked_fill(steps > hit_idx[:, None], float("-inf")).max(dim=-1).values[hit]
    return {
        "THP": 100.0 * hit.float().mean().item(),
        "RMSD": (rmsd.mean().item(), rmsd.std().item()),
        "ETS": (ets.mean().item(), ets.std().item()) if hit.any() else (float("nan"), float("nan")),
        "n_hit": int(hit.sum().item()),
    }


def print_metrics(samples, label):
    m = transition_path_metrics(samples)
    ets = f"{m['ETS'][0]:.2f} ± {m['ETS'][1]:.2f}" if m["n_hit"] else "-"
    print(f"{label:>26}:  THP {m['THP']:5.1f}%   RMSD {m['RMSD'][0]:.3f} ± {m['RMSD'][1]:.3f}   ETS {ets}")

class TransitionPathEvent(EqualityCondition):
    def __init__(self, sigma: float = 1e-1, beta: float = 1_000.0):
        super().__init__(sigma=sigma)
        self.beta = beta  # softmin sharpness; beta -> inf recovers the hard min
        self.register_buffer("R_B", R_B.clone())

    def residual(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        dist = torch.linalg.norm(x - self.R_B[None, :, None], dim=1)  # (B, L)
        # Soft min spreads the gradient over every step (weights softmax(-beta * dist)),
        # unlike a hard min, which only reaches the single closest step.
        closest = -torch.logsumexp(-self.beta * dist, dim=-1) / self.beta  # (B,)
        return closest[:, None, None]


condition = TransitionPathEvent(sigma=1e-5)
guidance = GuidanceMC(flow, condition, num_mc_samples=1, max_norm=1e1).to(device)
samples = sampler.sample(num_samples, guidance=guidance, num_steps=25, sde=True).detach()

print_metrics(prior_samples, "unbiased MD prior")
print_metrics(samples, "guided (TPS event)")
plot_on_landscape(samples, title="Guided transition paths");

docs.title: Noisy Double-Well Transition Path Sampling¶
docs.text:
This notebook conditions a stochastic process rather than a Gaussian process: latent Gaussian increments are pushed through an overdamped Langevin simulator, and guidance conditions the resulting paths on a rare transition event. It reproduces the synthetic double-well experiment of Seong et al., Transition Path Sampling with Improved Off-Policy Training of Diffusion Path Samplers (TPS-DPS, ICLR 2025), in which a particle follows

\[dR_t = -\nabla U(R_t)\,dt + \sqrt{2\gamma k_B \lambda}\;dW_t\]

in a 2D potential with two wells connected by two reaction channels. Unbiased simulation almost never crosses between the wells; instead of training a bias force as TPS-DPS does, we condition the unbiased path measure on reaching the target well with Monte-Carlo guidance, and recover diverse transition paths through both channels.

docs.title: 2. Configuration¶
docs.text: The physical constants are taken verbatim from the TPS-DPS paper (Appendix B.4) and its reference implementation: \(\Delta t = 0.01\), \(T = 10\) (1000 MD steps), temperature \(\lambda = 1200\,\mathrm{K}\) and \(k_B = 8.6173303\times 10^{-5}\), giving a per-step noise standard deviation \(\sqrt{2 k_B \lambda\, \Delta t} \approx 0.045\).

docs.title: 3. The Double-Well SDE¶
docs.text:
The potential (paper Eq. 46) is

\[U(x, y) = \tfrac{1}{6}\Big[\,4(1 - x^2 - y^2)^2 + 2(x^2 - 2)^2 + \big((x+y)^2 - 1\big)^2 + \big((x-y)^2 - 1\big)^2 - 2\,\Big],\]

with two global minima \(R_\mathcal{A} = (-1.118, 0)\) and \(R_\mathcal{B} = (+1.118, 0)\) and two saddle points at \((0, \pm 1)\), one per reaction channel. DoubleWellDualChannelMap integrates the Langevin SDE (paper Eq. 45, \(\gamma = m = 1\)) with Euler-Maruyama. The \((x, y)\) channels are coupled coordinates of one particle, so the map overrides _map and consumes the whole (B, 2, num_md_steps) tensor of Brownian increments; the particle starts deterministically at \(R_\mathcal{A}\), so each path has num_md_steps + 1 positions.

docs.title: 4. Prior Samples¶
docs.text:
We score paths with the three TPS-DPS metrics, each computed on the path truncated at its closest approach to \(R_\mathcal{B}\) (as in the reference implementation):

  • THP (target hit percentage): % of paths whose closest approach lies inside \(\mathcal{B} = \{R : \lVert R - R_\mathcal{B}\rVert < 0.5\}\).
  • RMSD: distance from the closest approach to \(R_\mathcal{B}\), averaged over all paths.
  • ETS (energy of the transition state): highest potential crossed before the closest approach, averaged over hitting paths (paper: \(\approx 1.4\)–\(1.7\), vs. saddle energy \(U = 1.0\)).

docs.title: 5. Condition on the Transition Event¶
docs.text: To turn the trapped prior into transition paths, condition on the particle reaching \(\mathcal{B}\) at some point along its path. TransitionPathEvent is an EqualityCondition whose residual is a soft minimum over time of the distance to \(R_\mathcal{B}\), mirroring the max-over-path relaxed indicator used as the TPS-DPS training reward. Guidance uses the SDE sampler; max_norm softly limits the guidance magnitude and trades THP against ETS (lower it for smoother, lower-ETS paths at the cost of hit rate).

class SIRMap(BaseMap):
    """Coupled (S, I, R) Euler simulator with latent-driven transmission and recovery rates."""

    def __init__(self, num_times: int, dt: float):
        super().__init__(
            latent_dim=num_times,
            output_shape=(num_times,),
            channels=3,
            device=device,
            dtype=torch.float64,
        )
        self.num_times = num_times
        self.dt = dt

    def _map(self, z: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """z: (B, 3, num_times) iid N(0, 1) -> (B, 3, num_times) (S, I, R) paths."""
        B, C, N = z.shape
        if C != 3 or N != self.num_times:
            raise ValueError(f"expected latent shape (B, 3, {self.num_times}), got {tuple(z.shape)}")

        sqrt_dt = self.dt ** 0.5
        beta_noise = torch.cumsum(z[:, 0, :] * sqrt_dt, dim=-1)
        gamma_noise = torch.cumsum(z[:, 1, :] * sqrt_dt, dim=-1)
        beta_t = 0.70 * torch.exp(0.32 * torch.tanh(0.35 * beta_noise))
        gamma_t = 0.25 * torch.exp(0.24 * torch.tanh(0.35 * gamma_noise))

        infected = 0.012 + 0.045 * torch.sigmoid(z[:, 2, 0])
        recovered = torch.zeros_like(infected)
        susceptible = 1.0 - infected - recovered

        s_path = [susceptible]
        i_path = [infected]
        r_path = [recovered]

        for k in range(self.num_times - 1):
            infection = beta_t[:, k] * susceptible * infected
            recovery = gamma_t[:, k] * infected
            susceptible = susceptible - infection * self.dt
            infected = infected + (infection - recovery) * self.dt
            recovered = recovered + recovery * self.dt
            s_path.append(susceptible)
            i_path.append(infected)
            r_path.append(recovered)

        return torch.stack(
            [torch.stack(s_path, dim=-1), torch.stack(i_path, dim=-1), torch.stack(r_path, dim=-1)],
            dim=1,
        )  # (B, 3, num_times)
class SIRMap(BaseMap): """Coupled (S, I, R) Euler simulator with latent-driven transmission and recovery rates.""" def __init__(self, num_times: int, dt: float): super().__init__( latent_dim=num_times, output_shape=(num_times,), channels=3, device=device, dtype=torch.float64, ) self.num_times = num_times self.dt = dt def _map(self, z: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor: """z: (B, 3, num_times) iid N(0, 1) -> (B, 3, num_times) (S, I, R) paths.""" B, C, N = z.shape if C != 3 or N != self.num_times: raise ValueError(f"expected latent shape (B, 3, {self.num_times}), got {tuple(z.shape)}") sqrt_dt = self.dt ** 0.5 beta_noise = torch.cumsum(z[:, 0, :] * sqrt_dt, dim=-1) gamma_noise = torch.cumsum(z[:, 1, :] * sqrt_dt, dim=-1) beta_t = 0.70 * torch.exp(0.32 * torch.tanh(0.35 * beta_noise)) gamma_t = 0.25 * torch.exp(0.24 * torch.tanh(0.35 * gamma_noise)) infected = 0.012 + 0.045 * torch.sigmoid(z[:, 2, 0]) recovered = torch.zeros_like(infected) susceptible = 1.0 - infected - recovered s_path = [susceptible] i_path = [infected] r_path = [recovered] for k in range(self.num_times - 1): infection = beta_t[:, k] * susceptible * infected recovery = gamma_t[:, k] * infected susceptible = susceptible - infection * self.dt infected = infected + (infection - recovery) * self.dt recovered = recovered + recovery * self.dt s_path.append(susceptible) i_path.append(infected) r_path.append(recovered) return torch.stack( [torch.stack(s_path, dim=-1), torch.stack(i_path, dim=-1), torch.stack(r_path, dim=-1)], dim=1, ) # (B, 3, num_times) In [5]: Copied! 
flow = GaussianIncrementFlow(map=SIRMap(num_times, dt), device=device)
sampler = IntegratorSampler(flow=flow)
prior_samples = sampler.sample(num_samples, num_steps=NUM_STEPS).detach()

class NoisyObservation(EqualityCondition):
    """Gaussian observations of `channels` at the masked times, with noise standard deviation `sigma`."""

    def __init__(self, observations: torch.Tensor, channels: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor, sigma: float):
        super().__init__(sigma=sigma)
        self.register_buffer("observations", observations)
        self.register_buffer("channels", channels)
        self.register_buffer("mask", mask)

    def residual(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        selected = x[:, self.channels][:, :, self.mask]
        target = self.observations[self.channels][:, self.mask]
        return selected - target[None, :, :]


data_condition = NoisyObservation(observations, obs_channels, obs_mask, sigma=OBS_NOISE)

class FastEpidemic(BinaryCondition):
    """Peak I above `peak_i`, final I below `final_i` and final R above `final_r`."""

    def __init__(self, peak_i: float, final_i: float, final_r: float, v: float = 1e-5, smooth_tau: float = 0.015):
        super().__init__(v=v)
        self.peak_i, self.final_i, self.final_r = peak_i, final_i, final_r
        self.smooth_tau = smooth_tau

    def smooth_eval_condition(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        infected = x[:, 1, :]
        recovered = x[:, 2, :]
        components = torch.stack(
            [
                smooth_max(infected, self.smooth_tau) - self.peak_i,
                self.final_i - infected[:, -1],
                recovered[:, -1] - self.final_r,
            ],
            dim=-1,
        )
        return components[:, None, :]  # (B, 1, 3)

docs.title: Stochastic SIR Epidemic Conditioning¶
docs.text:
This notebook reproduces the SIR row of Figure 4 in LatentFlow: A General Framework for Conditioning Stochastic Processes (Sharrock, Astfalck & Moss, 2026). A stochastic epidemic is written as the deterministic image of Gaussian innovations, which drive the time-varying rates of an SIR model:

\[\frac{dS}{dt} = -\beta_t\,S\,I,\qquad \frac{dI}{dt} = \beta_t\,S\,I - \gamma_t\,I,\qquad \frac{dR}{dt} = \gamma_t\,I.\]

The transmission rate \(\beta_t\) and recovery rate \(\gamma_t\) are modulated by latent Brownian paths, and the initial infected fraction is itself a latent draw. Guidance then conditions the outbreak on

  1. data: noisy observations of the infected fraction over the early window \(t \le 3\);
  2. an event: a fast epidemic that peaks high (peak \(I > 0.32\)) yet burns out (final \(I < 0.18\)) with a large final recovered fraction (final \(R > 0.62\));
  3. both at once.

Only the infected channel is ever constrained directly; the shared dynamics carry the information to \(S\) and \(R\).

docs.title: 2. Configuration¶
docs.text: The time grid is defined at module level so the map and the conditions can both read it. The second cell holds the plotting and event-rate helpers reused by every figure.

docs.title: 3. The Stochastic SIR Simulator¶
docs.text: SIRMap is the generator \(T_\vartheta\): it integrates the compartments with an explicit Euler step. The first two latent channels are accumulated into Brownian paths that modulate \(\beta_t\) and \(\gamma_t\), and the first entry of the third sets the initial infected fraction; because \((S, I, R)\) share these dynamics, the map consumes the whole (B, 3, num_times) latent tensor.

docs.title: 4. Prior¶
docs.text: GaussianIncrementFlow runs the flow over the iid Gaussian increments and pushes them through the map, so sampling it without guidance gives unconditioned prior outbreaks.

docs.title: 5. Conditioned on Data¶
docs.text: Take one prior outbreak as the "truth" and observe only its infected fraction at every other time point of the early window \(t \le 3\), with Gaussian noise of standard deviation \(0.01\). NoisyObservation is an EqualityCondition whose sigma is that noise level. The early growth of \(I\) fixes the transmission rate, which in turn constrains \(S\) and \(R\).

docs.title: 6. Conditioned on an Event¶
docs.text: Now condition on the fast-epidemic event alone. FastEpidemic is a BinaryCondition that stacks one margin per component (positive when satisfied), using a smooth log-sum-exp maximum for the peak; guidance must satisfy all three at once. Only a few percent of prior outbreaks do.

docs.title: 7. Conditioned on Both¶
docs.text: ProductCondition multiplies the two likelihoods, so guidance must follow the observed early growth and produce the fast epidemic.

docs.title: 8. Summary¶
docs.text: The four regimes side by side, as in Figure 4 of the LatentFlow paper. The same prior, flow and sampler are used throughout; only the condition changes.
